title: Compare objects based on their attributes.
objectives: Compare objects based on their attributes.
i_can: I can compare things. I can tell how things are the same or different.
language_objectives: Orally describe the attributes of objects. Orally describe similarities and differences between objects by using the phrases exactly the same, different, and the same, but.
key_questions: What are some ways that things can be the same?
ad_texts: ["Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: In this lesson, students consider multiple attributes to compare objects. If all the attributes are the same, the objects are exactly the same. If some attributes are the same but some are different, students use the same but … to describe the similarities and differences. Attention to attributes is foundational to sorting throughout this topic.

title: Classify objects into two categories.
objectives: Classify objects into two categories.
i_can: I can compare things. I can sort things.
language_objectives: Orally explain how objects are sorted into two groups by attribute.
key_questions: What are some ways you can sort?
ad_texts: ["Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: Once students can compare objects based on a specific attribute, they can create groups of objects that share an attribute (classification). At first the groups are sorted by simple, obvious attributes like color. In this lesson, students choose a way to sort objects and use words to share how they sorted. This lesson introduces the term sort.

title: Classify objects into two categories and count.
objectives: Classify objects into two categories and count.
i_can: I can sort things into two groups. I can count how many in each group.
language_objectives: Orally explain different ways to sort objects into two groups.
key_questions: What can we do to count correctly?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.", "Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration. [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: In this lesson, students continue to classify objects into groups with a focus on challenging attributes. They also ask and answer a natural question after creating a group—How many are in the group? One-to-one correspondence and an understanding of cardinality are the subject of discussion and practice. This lesson formalizes the term count.

title: Classify objects into three categories and count.
objectives: Classify objects into three categories and count.
i_can: I can sort things into three groups. I can count how many in each group.
language_objectives: Orally explain how objects are sorted into three groups. Orally count in standard order to tell how many objects are in each group.
key_questions: What does it mean to sort into groups?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10.", "Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1 AD1] Count to 10. [K.Mod1 AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: After some experience with classification, students are able to sort into more than two groups. In this lesson, students sort into three groups and count the number of objects in each group. They also record their sort on paper, an early example of modeling with mathematics (SMP.4).

title: Classify objects into three categories, count, and match to a numeral.
objectives: Classify objects into three categories, count, and match to a numeral.
i_can: I can sort and count things. I can find the matching number.
language_objectives: Orally explain how objects are sorted into groups, and match a numeral to each group. Read numerals and associate each numeral with a quantity, expressed as lyrics in a counting song.
key_questions: How can numbers help us?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0\u201310.", "Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD3] Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0–10. [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: Students are exposed to written numerals during the first four lessons, but they are formally introduced in lesson 5. Students sing “I Can Count”, a song that may be familiar from prekindergarten, to name the numerals and associate each with a quantity. They continue to sort and count objects, now matching a numeral to each group. This lesson introduces the term number.

title: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can show how I count a group of things.
language_objectives: With a partner, listen to and orally describe a strategy to count and record a collection of objects. Use terms such as sort, count, number, and strategies.
key_questions: What are some strategies, or things we can do, to help us count?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10.", "Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects.", "Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD1] Count to 10. [K.Mod1.AD4] Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects. [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: This lesson is an opportunity to gather formative assessment data as students use a counting collection to explore ways to count and represent a group of items. Students decide how to count, observe how others count, and discuss accurate counting • Count and bag collections (see strategies. This lesson introduces the term strategy. Materials section in the module resources).

title: Practice counting accurately.
objectives: Practice counting accurately.
i_can: I can count. I can match a number to show how many.
language_objectives: Orally count to see if there are enough of something. Through partner games, practice counting orally and reading to match a numeral to a set of objects.
key_questions: How do you know you have counted correctly?
ad_texts: ["Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0\u201310.", "Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects.", "Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD3] Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0–10. [K.Mod1.AD4] Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects. [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: Young students need plenty of practice to integrate number core components and to count accurately. Throughout this module, students will consider reasons to count and use numbers. The games in this lesson provide counting practice and reinforce the idea that counting is both useful and fun. This lesson introduces the term enough.

title: Count sets in linear, array, and scattered configurations.
objectives: Count sets in linear, array, and scattered configurations.
i_can: I can use a strategy to count. I can match a number to show how many.
language_objectives: Orally explain strategies for counting in different configurations. Orally count and identify the number that tells how many in each set.
key_questions: What strategies can you use to count correctly?
ad_texts: ["Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: In this lesson, students explore ways to count pictures when objects are in linear, array, or scattered configurations. They use the touch and count strategy and learn an alternative strategy called mark and count for when objects cannot be moved. This lesson introduces the terms line and notice.

title: Conserve number regardless of the arrangement of objects.
objectives: Conserve number regardless of the arrangement of objects.
i_can: I can count things. I can match a number to show how many. When I move things, I dont need to count them again.
language_objectives: Orally count and tell how many are in the same set of objects, presented twice in different configurations. Read numerals and identify the numeral that tells how many in each set.
key_questions: Do I have to count again when a group is moved?
ad_texts: ["Say how many without recounting when objects are rearranged."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD6] Say how many without recounting when objects are rearranged.
laag: In this lesson, students consider whether to recount a group of objects after they are moved. Repeated experiences of this type help students understand conservation, that the number of objects in a group stays the same regardless of their arrangement.

title: Count out a group of objects to match a numeral.
objectives: Count out a group of objects to match a numeral.
i_can: I can count out a group of things to match a number.
language_objectives: Orally explain strategies for counting out a given amount of objects.
key_questions: How can we remember when to stop counting?
ad_texts: ["Count out a given number of 1\u201310 objects from a larger group."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD9] Count out a given number of 1–10 objects from a larger group.
laag: Once students can count a group to answer a how many question, they are ready to create a group with a specific number of objects. In this lesson, students explore a new reason for counting: to create a group of a specific size.

title: Write numerals 1–3 to answer how many questions.
objectives: Write numerals 1–3 to answer how many questions.
i_can: I can write 1, 2, or 3 to show how many.
language_objectives: Write the numerals 1, 2, and 3 and identify missing numbers in an oral and written sequence up to 3. Read to identify numerals and orally explain why people write numerals.
key_questions: Why do we write numbers?
ad_texts: ["Write numbers from 0 to 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10.
laag: Students consider why people write numerals as they learn to write 1, 2, and 3. In this lesson, students count spoken words, something they cannot see or touch, and represent the number of words by writing a numeral.

title: Write numerals 4 and 5 to answer how many questions.
objectives: Write numerals 4 and 5 to answer how many questions.
i_can: I can write 4 or 5 to show how many.
language_objectives: Write the numerals 4 and 5 and identify missing numbers in an oral and written sequence up to 5. Read to identify numerals in the environment and orally describe them.
key_questions: Why do we write numbers?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10.", "Write numbers from 0 to 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD1] Count to 10. [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10.
laag: Students continue to explore reasons for writing numerals as they learn the formations for 4 and 5.

title: Count out enough objects and write the numeral.
objectives: Count out enough objects and write the numeral.
i_can: I can count out enough. I can write a number to show how many.
language_objectives: Orally describe strategies to determine if there are enough of something.
key_questions: How did you know you counted out enough?
ad_texts: ["Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects.", "Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD4] Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects. [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.
laag: In this lesson students think about the concept of enough and use it to see whether they have correctly counted out a group. Students pass out plates and serve pretend food to reason about making sure they have enough.

title: Understand the meaning of zero and write the numeral.
objectives: Understand the meaning of zero and write the numeral.
i_can: I can explain what zero means. I can write 0 and other numbers to show how many.
language_objectives: Write numerals including zero and orally describe the meaning of zero. Listen to a count and orally state the missing number.
key_questions: What does zero mean?
ad_texts: ["Write numbers from 0 to 10.", "Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0\u201310."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10. [K.Mod1.AD3] Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0–10.
laag: Students learn to use zero to describe a group with no objects. They watch a video that shows taking away one object at a time until there are no objects left and use beans to model what they see. Students also learn to write the numeral 0.

title: Sort the same group of objects in more than one way and count.
objectives: Sort the same group of objects in more than one way and count.
i_can: I can sort in different ways. I know the number of things stays the same even if the sort changes.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally describe strategies for sorting by attribute (including color and size), and explain how to show the totals and parts. Orally compare and connect each sort to a number sentence.
key_questions: Does sorting the same group a different way change the number of objects?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: Students count to find the total number of objects in a set and then sort the set into groups. They express the relationship between the total and the groups (or parts) by using a number sentence, such as 5 is 4 and 1. Students sort their set of objects more than once, by using a different attribute each time. This lesson introduces the phrase number sentence.

title: Decompose a set shown in a picture.
objectives: Decompose a set shown in a picture.
i_can: I can sort in different ways. I can write numbers about my sort.
language_objectives: Orally describe objects in a picture to classify them into two groups. Draw and write to represent an addition problem with both addends unknown.
key_questions: What are ways to break a set into groups? How can we make a number sentence to match a group?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Sort objects into categories."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD10] Sort objects into categories.
laag: Students sort objects in pictures by selecting an attribute and describing how many objects fit into each group. This is a new layer of abstraction as students cannot move the objects into groups. It focuses attention on the numbers in preparation for the part–total work in module 4.

title: Model story problems.
objectives: Model story problems.
i_can: I can show story problems in different ways.
language_objectives: Orally explain what happens when quantities are joined and when they are separated. Listen in order to model and solve add to and take from math story problems.
key_questions: What happens to a group when some join? What happens to a group when some leave?
ad_texts: ["This lesson is foundational to the work of K.OA.A.1. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module."]
ad_full: This lesson is foundational to the work of K.OA.A.1. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module.
laag: Children intuitively model story problems as part of their everyday lives. This lesson taps into their natural way of thinking about addition and subtraction problems. They learn that when more things come, the group gets bigger, and when things leave, the group gets smaller. Module 5 explores formal addition and subtraction conventions. This lesson introduces the terms explain and solve.

title: Model story problems and identify the numeral referents.
objectives: Model story problems and identify the numeral referents.
i_can: I can tell about a story problem. I can use number sentences.
language_objectives: Listen in order to model and solve story problems. Read and listen to a number sentence that matches the story problem, and orally explain what each number refers to.
key_questions: What is a story problem? What do number sentences tell us about a story problem?
ad_texts: ["This lesson is foundational to the work of K.OA.A.1. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module."]
ad_full: This lesson is foundational to the work of K.OA.A.1. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module.
laag: This lesson extends the intuitive modeling of story problems by helping students attach numbers to the context of the story. Understanding what numbers refer to in math stories is key to solving story problems successfully. Introducing problem-solving skills slowly throughout the year is intentional. Story problems are revisited in modules 4 and 5.

title: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can show how I count a group of things.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally describe strategies to accurately count and record a collection of objects, including move and count and touch and count.
key_questions: What are some strategies, or things we can do, to help us count?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10.", "Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects.", "Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD1] Count to 10. [K.Mod1.AD4] Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects. [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: This lesson invites students to count and record a collection of objects by using the tools and strategies of their choice. During this second experience with counting collections, students have an opportunity to demonstrate and celebrate growth with counting concepts while teachers gather formative assessment data. There is no fluency component in this lesson.

title: Count objects in 5-group and array configurations and match to a numeral.
objectives: Count objects in 5-group and array configurations and match to a numeral.
i_can: I can use a 5-group to count. I can match my count to a number.
language_objectives: Orally compare counting on fingers to counting in 5-group formations, and describe the relationship between models.
key_questions: What makes 5 an important number?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: Students relate counting the math way on their fingers to pictorial 5-group formations. These models allow students to see numbers 6–10 in relation to 5, which supports visualization and subitizing. Students will also create and count array configurations. The term 5-group is introduced in this lesson.

title: Count sets in circular configurations and match to a numeral.
objectives: Count sets in circular configurations and match to a numeral.
i_can: I can count things that are in a circle. I can match my count to a number.
language_objectives: Orally describe strategies to start, track, and end a count in a circular configuration, including mark and count. After finding the total in a set, read to identify the numeral that tells how many.
key_questions: What are some strategies, or things we can do, to help us count things that are in a circle?
ad_texts: ["Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0\u201310.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD3] Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0–10. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: Young students need plenty of practice to integrate number core components to count accurately. This is the first lesson where students consider how to accurately count objects in a circular configuration. They discuss strategies to track, start, and end their count.

title: Count sets in scattered configurations and match to a numeral.
objectives: Count sets in scattered configurations and match to a numeral.
i_can: I can use strategies to help me count. I can match my count to a number.
language_objectives: Orally describe how counting strategies differ for counting a group of concrete objects versus counting a group in a picture. Read numerals in isolation and orally count sets of objects while playing a game.
key_questions: Which strategy would you use to count a scattered group?
ad_texts: ["Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0\u201310.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD3] Represent a group of objects with a written numeral 0–10. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: Students count objects in scattered configurations by using move and count for concrete objects and mark and count for pictures. They match number cards to groups in scattered, circular, linear, and array configurations. Then they play bingo, which provides practice with recognizing numbers in isolation.

title: Conserve number regardless of the order in which objects are counted.
objectives: Conserve number regardless of the order in which objects are counted.
i_can: I can start counting things at different places. I know the number of things stays the same.
language_objectives: Orally count a number of objects by using different counting paths and explain why the total remains the same. Orally count, and then identify the number that tells how many orally and in writing.
key_questions: Does it matter where you start counting?
ad_texts: ["Say how many without recounting when objects are rearranged."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD6] Say how many without recounting when objects are rearranged.
laag: Students count groups of scattered objects in different ways. They notice that the number of objects stays the same. Students use repeated experiences to test the idea and confirm that the number of objects stays the same no matter the order in which they are counted.

title: Count out a group of objects to match a numeral.
objectives: Count out a group of objects to match a numeral.
i_can: I can count out a group of things to match a number.
language_objectives: Orally explain strategies for counting out a given amount of objects.
key_questions: How can we remember when to stop counting?
ad_texts: ["Count out a given number of 1\u201310 objects from a larger group."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD9] Count out a given number of 1–10 objects from a larger group.
laag: This lesson revisits the drive-thru role-play game from lesson 10, where students counted out a group of objects to match a number from 1–5. This lesson extends the work to 10. Now that students can accurately count a group of up to 10 objects and recognize numerals 6–10, they are ready to create larger groups.

title: Write numerals 6 and 7.
objectives: Write numerals 6 and 7.
i_can: I can write numbers up to 7 to show how many.
language_objectives: Write the numerals 6 and 7 and identify missing numbers in an oral and written sequence up to 7. Read to identify numerals and orally describe purposes for writing numerals.
key_questions: Why do we write numbers?
ad_texts: ["Write numbers from 0 to 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10.
laag: Students consider why people write numerals as they learn to write 6 and 7. They focus on writing numerals as a way to remember how many times something happens.

title: Write numeral 8.
objectives: Write numeral 8.
i_can: I can write numbers up to 8 to show how many.
language_objectives: Write the numeral 8 and identify missing numbers in an oral and written sequence up to 8. Read to identify numerals and orally explain purposes for writing numerals.
key_questions: Why do we write numbers?
ad_texts: ["to 10.", "Count", "Write numbers from 0 to 10."]
ad_full: to 10. [K.Mod1.AD1] Count [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10.
laag: Students know that written numerals tell how many, are more efficient than drawing, and help us remember quantities. They continue to explore reasons people write numerals as they learn to write 8. They realize, when counting the arms and legs of animals, it’s helpful to write down the number of limbs rather than count them over again.

title: Write numerals 9 and 10.
objectives: Write numerals 9 and 10.
i_can: I can write numbers up to 10 to show how many.
language_objectives: Write the numerals 9 and 10 and identify missing numbers in an oral and written sequence up to 10. Read to identify numerals and orally establish a purpose for writing numerals.
key_questions: Why do we write numbers?
ad_texts: ["Write numbers from 0 to 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD2] Write numbers from 0 to 10.
laag: Students round out their module 1 numeral writing experience by learning how to form 9 and 10. They celebrate their new abilities by writing numerals 1–10 in order and sharing their thoughts about why people write numerals.

title: Order numerals 1–10 and reason about an unknown number in the number sequence.
objectives: Order numerals 1–10 and reason about an unknown number in the number sequence.
i_can: I can put numbers in order. I can write numbers that are missing.
language_objectives: Read numerals and orally reason about how to put them in order. Listen to and orally describe how to check a number sequence for accuracy and identify missing numbers.
key_questions: How does number order help you figure out which number is missing?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD1] Count to 10.
laag: Sequencing numbers helps students begin to understand the relationship between them. Students explore this relationship by ordering Numeral Cards 1–10. They become number detectives by identifying numbers within the sequence that they can not see.

title: Model the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence.
objectives: Model the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence.
i_can: I can say the next number when I count. I can show that it is one more.
language_objectives: Orally explain the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence.
key_questions: What do you notice, or see and hear, as we count from 1 to 10?
ad_texts: ["Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD7] Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10.
laag: Students visualize the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence through a series of models. The number stairs are a high-impact visual to help students see that when counting forward, each number said is 1 more than the previous number.

title: Build number stairs to show the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence.
objectives: Build number stairs to show the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence.
i_can: I can count and write numbers in order. I can make number stairs to match.
language_objectives: Orally explain the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence. In writing, use the pattern of 1 more to record the structure of number stairs.
key_questions: What do you notice as we count from 1 to 10?
ad_texts: ["Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD7] Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10.
laag: Students build and draw number stairs to show the pattern of 1 more in the forward count sequence. They use their work to show how each successive number is 1 more and develop language to describe the pattern.

title: Model the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence.
objectives: Model the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence.
i_can: I can count back from 10 to 0. I can show the next number is one less.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally explain the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence.
key_questions: What do you notice as we count back from 10 to 0?
ad_texts: ["Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD7] Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10.
laag: Students see the pattern of 1 less while counting backward through a series of models. The final model is the number stairs flipped to start at 10. Using a familiar model helps students see that the pattern of 1 less is complementary to the pattern of 1 more and that when counting backward, each number said is 1 less than the previous number.

title: Build number stairs to show the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence.
objectives: Build number stairs to show the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence.
i_can: I can count back from 10 to 0. I can make number stairs to match.
language_objectives: Orally explain the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence. In writing, use the pattern of 1 less to record the structure of number stairs.
key_questions: What do you notice as we count back from 10 to 0?
ad_texts: ["Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD7] Recognize that each successive number is one more when counting within 10.
laag: Students build and draw number stairs from 10 to 1 to show the pattern of 1 less in the backward count sequence. They use their work to show that the next number is 1 less and develop language to describe the pattern.

title: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can show how I count a group of things.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally describe strategies to accurately count and record a collection of objects, including the use of drawings and numerals.
key_questions: How did you get better at counting and recording?
ad_texts: ["Count to 10.", "Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects.", "Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted.", "Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration."]
ad_full: [K.Mod1.AD1] Count to 10. [K.Mod1.AD4] Say one number name with each object when counting up to 10 objects. [K.Mod1.AD5] Use the last number of a count to tell how many regardless of arrangement or order counted. [K.Mod1.AD8] Count to answer how many questions about as many as 10 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, a circle, or a scattered configuration.
laag: This counting collection lesson serves as a culminating task for the module. Students notice that each stick has the same number of cubes and is the same length, even when the parts are different.

title: Compare weights by using heavier than, lighter than, and about the same weight as.
objectives: Compare weights by using heavier than, lighter than, and about the same weight as.
i_can: I can compare things. I can tell if one is heavier, lighter, or about the same weight as the other.
language_objectives: Orally compare weights of objects by using the phrases heavier than, lighter than, or about the same weight as.
key_questions: How can you tell whether an object is heavier or lighter than another object?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data Bigger or Equal?
ad_texts: ["Describe measurable attributes of an object.", "Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD3] Describe measurable attributes of an object. [K.Mod3.AD5] Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter.
laag: Students explore weight as a measurable attribute. They begin by holding two objects in their hands to see which feels heavier and making a comparison statement. They learn that a balance scale can be used to accurately compare weight. This lesson introduces the terms weight, heavy, and light.

title: Use a balance scale to compare two objects.
objectives: Use a balance scale to compare two objects.
i_can: I can use a balance scale to tell if one thing is heavier, lighter, or about the same weight as the other.
language_objectives: Orally explain how objects are sorted into two groups by attributes. Orally compare weights of objects by using the phrases heavier than or lighter than.
key_questions: How can you tell which object is heavier when you use a balance scale?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data Bigger or Equal?
ad_texts: ["Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD5] Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter.
laag: Students use a balance scale to compare the weights of two objects. They observe that the heavier objects go down on a balance scale while the lighter objects go up. They relate this to real world experiences with balance beams and seesaws. Students make comparison statements by using heavier than, lighter than, and about the same weight as.

title: Use a balance scale to compare an object to a group of cubes.
objectives: Use a balance scale to compare an object to a group of cubes.
i_can: I can use a balance scale to compare things to cubes. I can make the sides the same weight.
language_objectives: Listen to peer explanations in order to strategize about how to use a balance scale. State observations about the movement of the scale. Orally compare weights of objects by using the phrase is the same weight as.
key_questions: What does it mean when the sides of the scale are balanced?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data Bigger or Equal?
ad_texts: ["Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD5] Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter.
laag: Students use balance scales to find how many cubes are about the same weight as a classroom object. The cube serves as a weight unit in this lesson, foreshadowing the weight measurement that students do in grade 3. This lesson includes Math Past resources and provides students with insight into the origins of and uses for the balance scale over time.

title: Use a balance scale to compare an object to different units.
objectives: Use a balance scale to compare an object to different units.
i_can: I can use a balance scale to compare different things to another thing. I can make the sides the same weight.
language_objectives: Orally strategize how to balance the weight of two different types of objects on a balance scale and orally analyze the effects of adding or removing weight. Orally compare weights of different objects by using the phrase is the same weight as.
key_questions: What happens when you use different units to balance the same object?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data Bigger or Equal?
ad_texts: ["Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD5] Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter.
laag: This lesson opens a conversation about units that continues throughout elementary school. Students strategize to balance a scale, but this time they compare a single object with sets of different unit weights. Unit weights include cubes, beans, pennies, and other uniformly sized objects that can be easily found in great number.

title: Observe conservation of weight on the balance scale.
objectives: Observe conservation of weight on the balance scale.
i_can: I can weigh things. I can change somethings shape and tell why it weighs the same.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally reason about why the weight of the clay remains the same despite the change of its shape.
key_questions: What happens to the weight of an object when you change its shape?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data Bigger or Equal?
ad_texts: ["Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD5] Compare the weights of two objects directly and describe the difference with terms such as heavier or lighter.
laag: Once students are confident in their ability to balance objects on a balance scale, they are ready to explore conservation concepts. Students create two balls of clay that are about the same weight and reshape them. As they compare the new shapes, they see that the weight of the clay remains the same.

title: Relate more and fewer to length.
objectives: Relate more and fewer to length.
i_can: I can tell which one has more because it is longer. I can tell which one has fewer because it is shorter.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally compare lengths of name trains by using the phrases more than and fewer than.

title: Compare sets by using more than, fewer than, and the same number as.
objectives: Compare sets by using more than, fewer than, and the same number as.
i_can: I can choose how to compare things. I can tell which has more, fewer, or the same number as another.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally strategize about how to compare the number of objects in two groups. Orally make a comparison statement by using the terms more than, fewer than, and the same as.
key_questions: How can we compare the number of objects in two groups?
ad_texts: ["Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD1] Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies.
laag: This lesson focuses on strategies for comparing sets. Students choose a strategy and compare two groups of cubes to determine which has more or fewer. They evaluate the comparison strategies and decide whether the strategies work all the time or just sometimes.

title: Use number to compare sets with like units.
objectives: Use number to compare sets with like units.
i_can: I can use numbers to compare cube sticks.
language_objectives: Orally explain how cube sticks are sorted into two groups. With a partner, orally explain where to put the cubes on a number path by using the phrases more than and less than.
key_questions: How can the number path help us compare sets?
ad_texts: ["Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD1] Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies.
laag: Students compare sets as they sort number stairs into two groups: less than 5 and more than 5. After they sort the number stairs, students match each stair to a number on the number path. Use of the number path focuses students on number, which is a step toward comparing written numerals 1 to 10.

title: Classify flat shapes into groups and compare the number of shapes in each group.
objectives: Classify flat shapes into groups and compare the number of shapes in each group.
i_can: I can sort objects into groups. I can use numbers to put groups in order.
language_objectives: As a class, orally reason about which strategies would help to sort, compare, and order groups of shapes by using the phrases more and fewer. Orally compare and sequence groups of shapes from fewest to most.
key_questions: How can we compare the number of objects in groups when the objects aren’t the same size?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many?
ad_texts: ["Count the number of objects in each category of a sort and order the groups by count."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD6] Count the number of objects in each category of a sort and order the groups by count.
laag: Students review flat shapes and sorting concepts in the context of number comparison. They sort shapes of different sizes, compare the number of shapes in each group, and order the groups from fewest to most shapes. Because the units (shapes) vary in size, students must use a strategy other than comparing length to determine which group has more.

title: Count and compare sets with unlike units.
objectives: Count and compare sets with unlike units.
i_can: I can count and compare different things. I can share my strategy.
language_objectives: Orally share and listen to others share about the comparison of sets by using different strategies (such as matching items one by one, lining up objects on a number path, or filling in a 10-frame) in order to compare and connect strategies.
key_questions: How can we compare groups of different things?
ad_texts: ["Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD1] Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies.

title: Count and compare sets in pictures.
objectives: Count and compare sets in pictures.
i_can: I can use tools to help me count and compare things in pictures. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally share about comparing sets (including comparing length, by using the counting sequence, and matching objects along a number path). Listen to others share to compare and connect strategies.
key_questions: How can we compare two groups if we can’t align the objects?
ad_texts: ["Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD1] Compare the number of objects in two groups by using the terms more than, fewer than, or the same number as, e.g., by using matching or counting strategies.
laag: Comparing sets in pictures requires students to work abstractly and quantitatively. Sets are presented by using video and in photographs so that students cannot physically match up the objects. They select representative materials, drawings, or numbers and use them to determine which set has more.

title: Compare the capacity of containers by using numerals.
objectives: Compare the capacity of containers by using numerals.
i_can: I can count and compare the number of scoops that fill containers. I can tell which number is greater or less.
language_objectives: With a partner, compare the capacity of different containers by using the phrases greater than, less than, and equal to.
key_questions: When you compare numbers, how do you know which number is greater? Less?
ad_texts: ["Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD2] Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to.

title: Compare numbers by using greater than, less than, and equal to.
objectives: Compare numbers by using greater than, less than, and equal to.
i_can: I can tell when a number is greater than another number. I can tell when a number is less than another number.
language_objectives: Orally compare and sequence numerals by using the phrases greater than, less than, and equal to.
key_questions: How can we compare numbers without using sets of objects?
ad_texts: ["Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD2] Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to.
laag: Students move away from using concrete strategies for comparing sets toward using numerals. Students count and represent claps and stomps with a numeral. They look at numerals to compare the number of sounds in each group. They also play a game for continued practice with directly comparing numbers.

title: Compare two numbers in story situations.
objectives: Compare two numbers in story situations.
i_can: I can compare numbers from a story.
language_objectives: As a class, listen to math stories in order to make comparison statements. Orally compare embedded numbers in math stories by using the phrases greater than, less than, and equal to.
key_questions: When is it helpful to compare numbers?
ad_texts: ["Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to."]
ad_full: [K.Mod3.AD2] Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals by using the terms greater than, less than, or equal to.
laag: Students listen to short stories that incorporate numbers. They identify greater and less in a variety of situations and solve problems that involve comparing numbers.

title: Describe and compare several measurable attributes of objects and sets.
objectives: Describe and compare several measurable attributes of objects and sets.
i_can: I can compare things in different ways. I can use numbers to tell how I compare things.
language_objectives: Orally identify and name attributes to compare objects and select appropriate tools and strategies to make comparisons. Orally compare objects by using relevant vocabulary to make comparison statements (such as heavier when comparing weight and shorter when comparing length).
key_questions: What different ways can we compare objects?
big_idea: Sort and Describe Data How Many? Bigger or Equal?

objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can use math tools to show how I count a group of things.
language_objectives: Through listening and speaking, describe strategies to accurately count and record a collection of objects, including the use of 10-frames and number paths.

title: Compose flat shapes and count the parts.
objectives: Compose flat shapes and count the parts.
i_can: I can use smaller shapes to make larger shapes. I can count the parts.
language_objectives: Orally explain how the parts of a shape are composed to make the whole shape. Orally describe different ways to compose a shape.
key_questions: What is the same about the composite shapes? What is different about the composite shapes?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Making Shapes from Parts
ad_texts: ["Compose shapes to form larger shapes."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD5] Compose shapes to form larger shapes.
laag: Module 4 opens with the familiar concept of composing flat shapes. Students use the term parts to describe the simple shapes that form a larger composite shape, the whole. They see that there may be more than one way to compose a shape. This lesson introduces the terms part and whole.

title: Decompose flat shapes and count the parts.
objectives: Decompose flat shapes and count the parts.
i_can: I can take apart shapes to make smaller shapes. I can count the parts.
language_objectives: Orally explain how the parts of a shape are embedded within a larger shape. Orally describe different ways to decompose the same shape.
key_questions: How can a square be like a puzzle?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Making Shapes from Parts
ad_texts: ["Compose shapes to form larger shapes."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD5] Compose shapes to form larger shapes.
laag: Students decompose a square by cutting it, and then name the number and shape of the parts. They reassemble the squares by using new parts, which reinforces the idea that there may be more than one way to compose a shape or make a whole.

title: Decompose a group to identify parts and total.
objectives: Decompose a group to identify parts and total.
i_can: I can take apart a group. I can write a number sentence to show the parts and total.
language_objectives: Orally describe the parts and total in a contextual situation. Use a number sentence to orally explain the relationship between the parts and total.
key_questions: What is the total? What are the parts?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.
laag: This lesson transitions students from decomposing shapes to decomposing numbers. Students identify and circle parts in dot cards and in pictures to build their understanding of part–total relationships. Students complete sentence frames to represent their thinking numerically. This lesson introduces the term total.

title: Decompose a group and record parts and total by using a number bond.
objectives: Decompose a group and record parts and total by using a number bond.
i_can: I can take apart a group. I can show the parts and total with a number bond.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally explain how the parts and total in a contextual situation are related. Write to record the parts and total by using a number bond.
key_questions: Why do we use number bonds? How does a number bond help us see the parts and total?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.
laag: With a growing understanding of part–total relationships, students are ready for a tool to help them record all the parts they see within the total. This lesson introduces the number bond model. In this lesson, students use dot and picture scenes to find parts and total and record them in a number bond.

title: Sort to decompose a number in more than one way.
objectives: Sort to decompose a number in more than one way.
i_can: I can sort a group in different ways. I can show the same total with different numbers using a number bond.
language_objectives: Orally explain how a total can be sorted into parts in more than one way. Use a number bond and number sentence to orally explain the relationship between the parts and total.
key_questions: How can the same total be broken into different parts? Why do we use number bonds?
ad_texts: ["Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD4] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures.
laag: Using the familiar context of sorting, students decompose numbers in more than one way. They record their decompositions by using a number bond and compare their work. They consider how the same total can be made of different parts.

title: Decompose a number in more than one way and record.
objectives: Decompose a number in more than one way and record.
i_can: I can break apart the same total into different parts. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally describe how different parts can be combined to make a total by using the term partners to x. Use a number bond to orally explain the relationships between the parts and total.
key_questions: Which numbers can be parts of 6? Which numbers cannot be parts of 6?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.", "Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds. [K.Mod4.AD4] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures.
laag: Young students need substantial practice decomposing numbers that are less than or equal to 10 in more than one way. They learn to play Shake Those Disks, a game that provides decomposition practice and reinforces the idea that the same total can be broken into different parts. This lesson introduces the term partners to x.

title: Find partners to 5.
objectives: Find partners to 5.
i_can: I can find all partners to 5. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally analyze cube sticks, decomposed into various parts with a total of 5, to identify which cube stick is missing. Use number sentences to orally explain the relationships between all the different parts of the same total.
key_questions: Which numbers can be parts of 5? Which numbers cannot be parts of 5?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.", "Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds. [K.Mod4.AD4] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures.
laag: Students understand the idea that a total can be decomposed in more than one way and are ready to systematically decompose a number to find all the possible partners. 5 is a key starting point because the partners to 5 are subitizable for most students. This lesson is foundational to the kindergarten fluency goal of knowing sums and differences to 5.

title: Find partners to 10.
objectives: Find partners to 10.
i_can: I can find all partners to 10. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally determine a category in which three pictures belong. Use decompositions to 10 to justify why one picture does not fit. Orally explain how a total can be sorted into parts in more than one way. Use a number bond and number sentence to orally explain the relationship between partners to 10.
key_questions: Which numbers can be parts of 10? Which numbers cannot be parts of 10?
ad_texts: ["Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD4] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures.
laag: Students continue to use their sorting skills to decompose a number in more than one way, this time focusing on partners to 10. Students break 10 into two or more parts and record their work by using a number bond.

title: Compose shapes in more than one way.
objectives: Compose shapes in more than one way.
i_can: I can use different parts to make the same shape. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally compare different ways to compose a shape puzzle. Orally explain how many parts make up the whole when composing shapes in more than one way.
key_questions: Why can different parts be used to make the same whole shape? Why can different parts be used to make the same total?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Making Shapes from Parts
ad_texts: ["Compose shapes to form larger shapes."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD5] Compose shapes to form larger shapes.
laag: This lesson returns to shape work to solidify the idea that a whole or total can be composed in multiple ways. In topic A, students compared their work and began to notice that shapes can be composed in more than one way. Now they are ready to independently compose the same shape more than once. They relate shape and number composition in Land by answering the same key question for both units.

title: Sort and record the decomposition with a number bond.
objectives: Sort and record the decomposition with a number bond.
i_can: I can sort objects into groups. I can show the parts and total with a number bond.
language_objectives: Orally share strategies for sorting in different ways and for recording to show the totals and parts. Orally compare sorts and connect each to a number bond.
key_questions: How do you find the total and the parts in a number bond?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.
laag: Throughout the topic, students decomposed numbers and shapes in multiple ways and recorded their thinking. In this lesson, students demonstrate and celebrate growth with part–total thinking as they choose a way to sort, or decompose, a group of objects and record by using a number bond. The class discusses multiple ways that a sort can be represented. This lesson presents an opportunity to gather formative assessment data about student understanding of part–total thinking and representations.

title: Model put together with total unknown story problems.
objectives: Model put together with total unknown story problems.
i_can: I can show what happens in a story. I can show the parts and total.
language_objectives: Represent a put together with total unknown story problem and orally identify the parts and total. Use number bonds to orally explain the relationships between the parts and total.
key_questions: Do story problems have parts and a total? How do you know?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.", "Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds. [K.Mod4.AD2] Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool.
laag: This lesson represents a transition in part–total thinking. In topics A and B, students usually started with a total and decomposed it to find the parts. When working with put together with total unknown stories, the parts are given and students compose to find the total.

title: Draw to represent put together with total unknown story problems.
objectives: Draw to represent put together with total unknown story problems.
i_can: I can draw to show what happens in a story. I can show the parts and total with a number bond.
language_objectives: Listen to a story problem to orally identify the parts and total in the problem. Orally explain the relationship between the parts and total shown in a number bond.
key_questions: What is a math drawing? How can math drawings help us solve problems?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD2] Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool.
laag: Students learn the difference between art and math drawings. They understand that they can make math drawings to show a story problem that they visualize. Students use math drawings to model and solve.

title: Choose a math tool to solve put together with total unknown story problems.
objectives: Choose a math tool to solve put together with total unknown story problems.
i_can: I can choose tools to show what happens in a story. I can show the parts and total.
language_objectives: Orally share strategies to solve put together with total unknown story problems (including modeling with cubes and a number bond and modeling with a drawing) to show the totals and parts. Orally compare and connect each strategy to a number bond. Orally justify how the choice of a math tool is helpful in solving story problems. Explain how math tools are used to show thinking.
key_questions: What math tools did you use to show your thinking? How did the math tools help you show your thinking?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD2] Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool.
laag: Students continue to solve put together with total unknown story problems. This lesson focuses on choosing and using math tools such as cubes, number bonds, drawings, and 10-frames.

title: Model take apart with both addends unknown situations.
objectives: Model take apart with both addends unknown situations.
i_can: I can break apart the same total in different ways in a story.  I can show the parts and total with a number bond.
language_objectives: Listen to a story problem and orally explain how to decompose the same total in different ways. Orally describe all the ways to decompose 7 by using number bonds and explain the relationships between the parts and total.
key_questions: Which numbers can be parts of 7? What do you notice about the numbers that are not part of 7?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD3] Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds.
laag: Take apart with both addends unknown situations provide a total and ask students to come up with possibilities for the parts. This is the most open-ended of the situation types, and most similar to the decomposition work from topics A and B. In this lesson, students model this situation type to find all the possible partners to 7.

title: Choose a math tool to solve take apart with both addends unknown situations.
objectives: Choose a math tool to solve take apart with both addends unknown situations.
i_can: I can choose tools to show what could happen in a story.  I can show the parts and total with a number bond.
language_objectives: Orally share strategies for solving take apart with both addends unknown story problems, including by modeling with cubes and a number bond and by modeling with a drawing. Orally compare strategies and connect each strategy to a number sentence.
key_questions: What is different about add to with result unknown and take apart with both addends unknown situations? Can we use the same math tools to show different types of situations?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds.", "Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD1] Represent composition or decomposition of numbers with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, or number bonds. [K.Mod4.AD3] Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds.
laag: Students show take apart with both addends unknown stories by acting out a series of stories and choosing math tools to model one story. The class discusses what numbers can be part of 8, by using their previous work with parts of 5, 6, 7, and 10 to help their reasoning. Students reflect on the differences between add to with result unknown and take apart with both addends unknown situations.

title: Compose and decompose numbers and shapes.
objectives: Compose and decompose numbers and shapes.
i_can: I can show parts and the total in stories, pictures, and shapes with a number bond.
language_objectives: As a class, orally reason about examples and nonexamples of number pairs to find all the partners to 9. Orally identify parts and totals by using shapes, pictures, and stories.
key_questions: What have you learned about parts and total? What math tools can you use to show your thinking about parts and totals, or wholes?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool.", "Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD2] Solve put together and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 with a chosen math tool. [K.Mod4.AD3] Record solutions to story situations in which both addends are unknown with objects, drawings, or number bonds.
laag: The activities in this lesson are presented as stations and serve as culminating tasks for the module. Students demonstrate and celebrate their growth with composition and decomposition of shapes and numbers. Take the opportunity to gather formative assessment data. There is no Fluency component in this lesson.

title: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can sort a group of things in different ways to help me count. I can show how I counted my collection.
language_objectives: Orally describe strategies to accurately count and record a collection of objects, including by sorting into two or more parts. Listen to others share their strategies to compare and connect them.
key_questions: How can sorting a collection help us count?
ad_texts: ["This lesson supports K.CC.1-5, the counting and writing numeral standards. These concepts build from the work in module 1 and get more sophisticated as the counting quantities get larger in subsequent modules. This content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module."]
ad_full: This lesson supports K.CC.1-5, the counting and writing numeral standards. These concepts build from the work in module 1 and get more sophisticated as the counting quantities get larger in subsequent modules. This content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module.
laag: This lesson invites students to count and record a collection of objects by using tools and strategies of their choice. Students demonstrate and celebrate growth with counting concepts and written recordings while teachers gather formative assessment data. Class discussion focuses on sorting and counting parts, as well as finding the total number of objects in the collection. There is no Fluency component in this lesson.

title: Use the structure of 5 and 10 to build a rekenrek.
objectives: Use the structure of 5 and 10 to build a rekenrek.
i_can: I can build a rekenrek. I can use what I know about 5 and 10 to show numbers on the rekenrek.
language_objectives: Orally explain how a number is represented on a rekenrek by identifying the color change at 5 beads.
key_questions: How does the rekenrek help you see or show numbers quickly and easily?
ad_texts: ["Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures."]
ad_full: [K.Mod4.AD4] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way by using objects or pictures.
laag: Students consider the organization of a rekenrek and create their own version of the tool by using pony beads. The organization of the rekenrek makes it easier for students to subitize and efficiently show numbers. There is no Fluency component in this lesson.

title: Represent add to with result unknown story problems by using drawings and numbers.
objectives: Represent add to with result unknown story problems by using drawings and numbers.
i_can: I can tell or draw an addition story. I can write a number sentence to match.
language_objectives: Listen to a story problem and orally describe the parts and the total in the problem. Use a number sentence to orally explain the relationship between the parts and the total by using the terms plus and equals.
key_questions: What happens when we put things together, or add?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
laag: Students use drawings and number sentences to represent add to with result unknown story problems. They transition from reading number sentences as “1 and 2 make 3” to “1 plus 2 equals 3.” Students recontextualize the number sentence by using it to tell the story. This lesson introduces the terms plus and addition and advances the term equals.

title: Relate number sentences and number bonds through story problems.
objectives: Relate number sentences and number bonds through story problems.
i_can: I can tell an addition story. I can show the parts and total with a number bond and a number sentence.
language_objectives: Orally compare parts and their total in a number bond and in a number sentence within a math story.
key_questions: How do number sentences and number bonds help us tell math stories? How are number sentences and number bonds the same?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
laag: In this lesson students relate the parts and total of a number bond to the parts and total of a number sentence. Students realize that number bonds and number sentences are ways to represent math stories, and that they can identify the parts and total in both representations.

title: Represent and solve add to with result unknown story problems.
objectives: Represent and solve add to with result unknown story problems.
i_can: I can tell an addition story. I can choose tools to help me solve it. I can write a number sentence to match.
language_objectives: Orally describe the parts and total of a math story by using a number sentence and a math tool. Orally compare strategies for solving story problems (including fingers, 10-frames, and drawings) by showing the totals and parts. Orally explain how a number sentence matches a story context by describing the parts and total.
key_questions: How can a number sentence help us tell a story?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.", "Solve add to, take from, put together, and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 by using addition and subtraction.", "Add and subtract within 10 by using objects, drawings, or other math tools."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations. [K.Mod5.AD4] Solve add to, take from, put together, and take apart with result unknown story problems within 10 by using addition and subtraction. [K.Mod5.AD6] Add and subtract within 10 by using objects, drawings, or other math tools.
laag: In this lesson, the class writes a story problem based on a video. After students solve the problem by using tools of their choice, they write a number sentence to match. They use the number sentences to show their solution and retell the math story. Students compare solution strategies and tools for solving addition problems.

title: Represent decomposition situations by using number bonds and addition sentences.
objectives: Represent decomposition situations by using number bonds and addition sentences.
i_can: I can sort the same total into different parts. I can show the parts and total with a number bond and a number sentence.
language_objectives: Use a number bond and a number sentence to orally explain the relationship between a total and its parts. Orally describe different ways a total can be decomposed into parts.
key_questions: How can the same total be made of different parts?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.", "Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way and record with equations such as 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations. [K.Mod5.AD7] Decompose numbers within 10 into pairs in more than one way and record with equations such as 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1.
laag: Students decompose a group and represent the situation with number bonds and addition sentences. Students begin with a total number of objects and then sort to create the parts, rather than beginning with the parts as they did for add to with result unknown problems. This naturally leads to recording the total on the left (e.g., 7 4 3). = +

title: Represent take apart with both addends unknown situations with a number sentence.
objectives: Represent take apart with both addends unknown situations with a number sentence.
i_can: I can break the total in a math story into parts. I can show the parts and total with a number sentence.
language_objectives: Orally describe the total and the parts in a math story by using drawings and number sentences. As a class, orally justify why the same total can have different parts.
key_questions: Why can the same total have different parts? What happens to the total when zero is a part?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
laag: Students continue to work with decomposition situations by representing a take apart with both addends unknown story. The story provides a total and students decide how to separate it into groups. Their number sentences also begin with a total.

title: Tell addition story problems starting from number sentence models.
objectives: Tell addition story problems starting from number sentence models.
i_can: I can tell a math story to match a number sentence. I can match number sentences and pictures.
language_objectives: Orally generate a story context from the numbers and operations in a number sentence. In groups, orally explain how a number sentence matches a story context by describing the parts and the total.
key_questions: How do you know when a number sentence matches a story or a picture?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
laag: Students solidify their understanding of the relationship between a number sentence and a story context. In previous lessons, they began with a story and wrote number sentences to match. In this lesson, they begin with a number sentence and tell a story to match. This directs attention to the structure of the number sentence, requiring students to identify the parts and total to develop or identify a matching story.

title: Find the total in an addition sentence.
objectives: Find the total in an addition sentence.
i_can: I can choose a tool to help me find a total. I can write an addition sentence with that total.
language_objectives: Orally share strategies for finding the total of a two-part expression (including using cubes, 10-frames, fingers, number paths, and drawings). Orally compare and connect each strategy to a number sentence.
key_questions: How can you add when there is no story?
big_idea: Being Flexible Within 10 Model with Numbers
ad_texts: ["Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.", "Add fluently within 5."]
ad_full: [K.Mod5.AD2] Represent addition with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations. [K.Mod5.AD9] Add fluently within 5.
