ad_full: [1.Mod1.AD4] Add fluently within 10. [1.Mod1.AD5] Fluently decompose totals within 10 in more than one way.
laag: In this lesson students build upon the previous lesson by finding the expressions for a given total. They apply the same systematic approach by using two-color counters to model the parts that make totals of 7 and 8. They record the finite set of two-part expressions equal to 7 and 8 and play a game to develop fluency with these facts.

title: Find all two-part expressions equal to 9 and 10.
objectives: Find all two-part expressions equal to 9 and 10.
i_can: I can show all the ways that two parts make 9 or 10.
language_objectives: Orally describe different ways to make 9 or 10 and write number sentences to match. Identify patterns when finding all two-part expressions equal to 9 or 10, and orally explain how the patterns help ensure every possible combination was found.
key_questions: How can we use the pattern on the Addition Totals chart to be sure that we found all the ways to make 9? 10?
ad_texts: ["Add fluently within 10.", "Fluently decompose totals within 10 in more than one way."]
ad_full: [1.Mod1.AD4] Add fluently within 10. [1.Mod1.AD5] Fluently decompose totals within 10 in more than one way.
laag: Students now decompose 9 and 10 to complete the lesson trio: 20, 21, and 22. As in earlier lessons, students use two-color counters to systematically model the finite set of two-part expressions equal to totals of 9 and 10. They record the expressions and develop fluency with the facts by playing a game.

title: Find the totals of doubles +1 facts.
objectives: Find the totals of doubles +1 facts.
i_can: I can find the total. I can use a doubles fact to help.
language_objectives: Explain orally and in writing how to use a doubles fact to find the total of a doubles +1 fact.
key_questions: How can a doubles fact help us find the total of a doubles +1 fact?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or by creating an equivalent but easier problem. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod1.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or by creating an equivalent but easier problem. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: The introduction of doubles in topic B and continued fluency practice have prepared students for the concepts in this lesson. Students recognize doubles facts through analyzing a series of pictures. They discover that they can use doubles facts to help them find doubles +1 facts. They apply these understandings to a sequence of related doubles and doubles +1 problems.

title: Use known facts to make easier problems.
objectives: Use known facts to make easier problems.
i_can: I can use facts to help me add numbers. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally describe addition strategies, including using known facts to make easier problems, and compare and connect addition strategies.
key_questions: How can we be sure that when we make an easier problem the total stays the same?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or by creating an equivalent but easier problem. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)", "Determine whether addition and/or subtraction number sentences are true or false."]
ad_full: [1.Mod1.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or by creating an equivalent but easier problem. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6) [1.Mod1.AD6] Determine whether addition and/or subtraction number sentences are true or false.
laag: Students apply the skill of breaking up an addend to use doubles for finding the totals of doubles +1 facts. They share and discuss various strategies for adding, including breaking up an addend to make the problem easier.

title: Organize, count, and record a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and record a collection of objects.
i_can: I can show how I count objects.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally describe a strategy with a partner to estimate, count, and record a collection of objects.
key_questions: How can we use groups to help us organize and count?
ad_texts: ["This lesson is foundational to the work of 1.NBT.A.1. Lesson content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module."]
ad_full: This lesson is foundational to the work of 1.NBT.A.1. Lesson content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in this module.
laag: This student-driven lesson invites partners to count and record a collection of objects by using tools and strategies of their choice. Through comparing and connecting strategies, students recognize the value of organizing objects into groups to count efficiently. Students may display a range of abilities. Due to the time needed to count collections, Fluency, Problem Set, and Exit Ticket are not included in this lesson. Use student recordings to analyze their work. There is no Exit Ticket for this lesson. Instead, use students’ recordings to analyze their work after the lesson.

title: Represent result unknown problems and record as addition or subtraction number sentences.
objectives: Represent result unknown problems and record as addition or subtraction number sentences.
i_can: I can write a number sentence to match a story. I can show how I add or subtract.
language_objectives: Listen to, read, model, and generate addition and subtraction result unknown story problems, and write number sentences to match. Orally explain why addition or subtraction is used to solve each problem and how each operation affects the total.
key_questions: How do we know when to add or when to subtract? What happens to the total when we add? What happens to the total when we subtract?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students watch a video of a school bus picking up and dropping off people and consider whether the action in each situation shows addition or subtraction. They use concrete and pictorial representations to model more bus stories, and they record and discuss corresponding number sentences.

title: Subtract all or subtract 0.
objectives: Subtract all or subtract 0.
i_can: I can subtract all or subtract 0. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Listen to, model, and generate problems that involve subtracting all or subtracting 0, and find the difference. Orally conjecture about patterns when subtracting all or subtracting 0.
key_questions: What happens when we subtract 0 from a number? What happens when we subtract all from a number?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)", "Subtract fluently within 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6) [1.Mod2.AD5] Subtract fluently within 10.
laag: Students solve problems that involve subtracting all or subtracting 0. They notice and discuss patterns in related problems. They generate statements that describe the results of subtracting all or subtracting 0 and try out those statements on new problems. They use these generalizations to help them solve related problems more efficiently.

title: Subtract 1 or subtract 1 less than the total.
objectives: Subtract 1 or subtract 1 less than the total.
i_can: I can subtract 1 or subtract 1 less than the total. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Listen to, model, and generate problems that involve subtracting 1 or subtracting 1 less than the total, and find the difference. Orally conjecture about patterns when subtracting 1 or subtracting 1 less than the total.
key_questions: What happens when we subtract 1? What happens when we subtract 1 less than the total?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)", "Subtract fluently within 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6) [1.Mod2.AD5] Subtract fluently within 10.
laag: Students solve problems that involve subtracting 1 or subtracting 1 less than the total. Students notice and discuss patterns in related problems to generate statements that describe the results of subtracting 1 from a number or subtracting 1 less than the total and try out those statements on new problems. They use these generalizations to help them solve related problems more efficiently.

title: Use fingers to subtract 4, 5, and 6 efficiently.
objectives: Use fingers to subtract 4, 5, and 6 efficiently.
i_can: I can take away 4, 5, or 6 all at once to help me subtract.
language_objectives: Through listening and speaking, model story problems by using fingers to take away all at once. Orally compare the efficiency of taking away all at once with other subtraction strategies.
key_questions: How can we solve subtraction problems efficiently?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)", "Subtract fluently within 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6) [1.Mod2.AD5] Subtract fluently within 10.
laag: Students model subtraction school bus stories by taking away 4, 5, and 6 fingers all at once. The focus of the lesson is on the efficiency of using fingers to subtract these subtrahends. All the minuends are within 10 to maximize finger work and fluency with these basic subtraction facts.

title: Use the Read–Draw–Write process to solve result unknown problems.
objectives: Use the Read–Draw–Write process to solve result unknown problems.
i_can: I can use Read-Draw-Write to help me solve story problems.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve result unknown story problems, and orally describe how each step helps to solve them. Orally compare addition and subtraction story problems and describe how drawing helps determine the operation.
key_questions: What process can we use to solve word problems? How can drawing help us figure out a way to solve?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students learn an introductory version of the Read–Draw–Write process to solve problems. Students use Read–Draw–Write to make sense of, represent, and solve familiar add to and take from with result unknown word problems. Finally, students reflect on their work by contrasting addition and subtraction word problems.

title: Represent and solve related addition and subtraction result unknown problems.
objectives: Represent and solve related addition and subtraction result unknown problems.
i_can: I can add or subtract. I can show the parts and total with a number sentence.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve result unknown story problems. Orally explain how a number sentence or number bond represents the problem. Orally make a generalization that addition and subtraction problems can have the same number bond when they have the same parts and total.
key_questions: Does the unknown represent a part or the total? Why can an addition problem and a subtraction problem have the same number bond?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students practice using the Read–Draw–Write (RDW) process as they solve add to with result unknown and take from with result unknown word problems. Working with related addition and subtraction problems allows the class to compare the representations for each operation. Through a study of number bonds, students discover that related problems have the same parts and total but that the unknowns represent either a part or a total.

title: Count on or count back to solve related addition and subtraction problems.
objectives: Count on or count back to solve related addition and subtraction problems.
i_can: I can count on or count back to solve problems with the same numbers. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model story problems by using a number path and drawings. Orally explain how addition and subtraction story problems that have the same parts and the same total are related.
key_questions: What makes two number sentences related, or similar?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod2.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students watch a video and notice what happens when the same amount is added to and then subtracted from a given number. They solve a series of problems like the ones in the video and discuss how the problems are related. They count on or count back to add and subtract.

title: Interpret and find an unknown change.
objectives: Interpret and find an unknown change.
i_can: I can count on to find how many I need. I can write a number sentence to match.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve unknown change story problems. Through whole class and partner discussions, count on to solve. Orally describe the steps taken to count on to find the unknown part, and explain how the process is different from counting on to find the unknown total.
key_questions: What is different about counting on to find a total and counting on to find an unknown part?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students count on to solve problems in which the unknown, for the first time in grade 1, is a part rather than the total. They use concrete tools and an everyday context that represents the known addend (I have) and the total (I want) to find an unknown addend (I need). Students start with the known part, count on until they get to the total, and then identify how many they counted on. The class writes an addition number sentence to match.

title: Represent and solve add to with change unknown problems.
objectives: Represent and solve add to with change unknown problems.
i_can: I can find how many more were added to get to the total. I can write a number sentence to match.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve add to with change unknown story problems. Through whole class and partner discussions, explain how a drawing helps to model a story problem and why labels are used.
key_questions: What are some ways to find an unknown part that was added?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students analyze an add to with change unknown situation and recognize that the unknown is a part that represents a change in quantity. They self-select tools to help them solve for the unknown, and then they share various solution strategies. Students study a sample drawing that represents the problem and discuss the value of using labels. They add labels to their own drawings and write number sentences and statements to complete their work.

title: Represent and find an unknown addend in equations.
objectives: Represent and find an unknown addend in equations.
i_can: I can count on to find a part. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve add to with change unknown story problems. Orally and in writing, generate add to with change unknown equations, count on to find the unknown part, and compare counting on with different tools. Orally evaluate the usage of different math tools for counting on.
key_questions: What is the same about counting on with different tools? Which tool is most helpful for you when you count on, and why?
ad_texts: ["Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD7] Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation.
laag: For the first time, students find the unknown in an equation. The equations are presented without the support of word problem contexts. Students use the count on strategy, which is familiar from work with word problems, to find unknown addends. The term equation is introduced in this lesson.

title: Represent and solve take from with change unknown problems.
objectives: Represent and solve take from with change unknown problems.
i_can: I can find the part that was taken away. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally model and compare add to and take from with change unknown story problems. Read, listen, draw, and write to solve take from with change unknown story problems.
key_questions: What are some ways to find a part that was taken away?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students connect to previous learning by comparing an add to with change unknown word problem with a take from with change unknown word problem. They concretely represent and solve a take from with change unknown problem and then draw to solve similar problems. Students discuss the meaning of the unknown, which is a subtrahend, for the first time.

title: Represent and find an unknown subtrahend in equations.
objectives: Represent and find an unknown subtrahend in equations.
i_can: I can find the unknown part. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally describe ways to find an unknown subtrahend, and listen to compare and connect the different strategies that are shared. Read, draw, and write to solve take from with change unknown story problems.
key_questions: What are some ways to find the unknown part? Which way is most efficient for you?
ad_texts: ["Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD7] Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation.
laag: Students reason about take from with change unknown situations and discuss different ways to represent these problems. They work with equations to find unknown subtrahends, counting back from the total to the known part. They use their fingers as well as the number path to keep track of the count and find the answer.

title: Represent and solve add to and take from with change unknown problems.
objectives: Represent and solve add to and take from with change unknown problems.
i_can: I can add or subtract to solve a story problem. I can use a number sentence to show how I know.
language_objectives: Through whole class and partner discussions, explain how to choose an operation and solve add to and take from with change unknown story problems. Read, listen to, retell, and model add to and take from with change unknown story problems.
key_questions: Should we write an addition or subtraction equation to represent the story? How do you know?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod2.AD7] Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation.
laag: Students watch videos and read word problems that depict add to and take from changes. Partners represent each situation with an addition or subtraction equation. They use a box to show the unknown in the equation and then solve. A game provides hands-on mixed practice with add to and take from situations.

title: Represent and solve put together/take apart with addend unknown problems.
objectives: Represent and solve put together/take apart with addend unknown problems.
i_can: I can add or subtract to find the unknown part.
language_objectives: Read, listen, draw, and write to solve put together/take apart with addend unknown story problems by using a number bond. Orally share and compare solution strategies, including counting on and counting back. Explain why both addition and subtraction work to find the unknown addend.
key_questions: How are counting on and counting back to find the unknown part the same and different? Why do addition and subtraction both work for finding the unknown part?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.
laag: Students solve a put together/take apart with addend unknown problem. They discuss the strategies of counting on and counting back to find the unknown. Students represent those strategies by using a number path and addition and subtraction equations. Then they make a number bond to model the relationship between addition and subtraction.

title: Relate counting on and counting back to find an unknown part.
objectives: Relate counting on and counting back to find an unknown part.
i_can: I can count on or count back to find the unknown part.  I can show how I know.
language_objectives: While playing a partner game and in a whole class discussion, listen to and model put together/take apart with addend unknown problems, and find the unknown by counting on and counting back. Orally compare number bonds, number paths, and number sentences to a story context.
key_questions: Why can we count on or count back to find an unknown part?
ad_texts: ["Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD7] Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation.
laag: Students count on and count back to find an unknown part. They use number paths and number sentences to show their strategies, and they use number bonds to record the part–total relationships. Students use these representations to discuss how the count on and count back strategies are connected.

title: Compare the efficiency of counting on and counting back to subtract.
objectives: Compare the efficiency of counting on and counting back to subtract.
i_can: I can decide to count on or count back to subtract. I can tell why.
language_objectives: Orally count on or count back to find an unknown part and compare the efficiency of each strategy.
key_questions: What helps us decide if we should count on or count back to solve?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on or back. (1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students count on and count back to find the value of an unknown part. They relate the size of the known part to the total to determine which counting strategy is more efficient.

title: Use related addition facts to subtract from 10.
objectives: Use related addition facts to subtract from 10.
i_can: I can use partners to 10 to help me subtract. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally explain how related addition facts help to efficiently find the unknown part when subtracting from 10.
key_questions: How can we use addition to solve subtraction problems efficiently?
ad_texts: ["Subtract by using think addition strategies."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD3] Subtract by using think addition strategies.
laag: Students study the artwork on the cover of the student book. They share strategies for solving a subtraction problem based on the painting. This discussion leads to using related addition facts to subtract from 10. The work is supported with number bonds to highlight the part–total relationships. Practice then transitions to simply thinking of the related addition fact, or partner to 10.

title: Use related addition facts to subtract.
objectives: Use related addition facts to subtract.
i_can: I can use addition to help me subtract. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Through whole class and partner discussion, orally explain how related addition facts help to efficiently find the unknown part in a subtraction problem within 10.
key_questions: How can we use addition to solve subtraction problems efficiently?
ad_texts: ["Subtract by using think addition strategies."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD3] Subtract by using think addition strategies.
laag: Students generate related addition and subtraction facts by using partners to 6. They discuss how using addition facts or thinking about which parts go together to make a total can help them solve subtraction problems efficiently. They practice these ideas by using totals of 6, 7, 8, and 9.

title: Determine the value of the unknown in various positions.
objectives: Determine the value of the unknown in various positions.
i_can: I can find the unknown part or total. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Through whole class and partner discussion, orally share strategies used to determine whether a number belongs in an equation with an unknown. Orally explain how number sentences are related by using part–whole understanding, and determine whether there are always four addition and subtraction number sentences that can be written for the same two parts and total.
key_questions: How can we find the value of the unknown in an addition or a subtraction equation?
ad_texts: ["Subtract by using think addition strategies.", "Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD3] Subtract by using think addition strategies. [1.Mod2.AD7] Find the unknown in an addition or subtraction equation.
laag: Students reason about which numbers make equations true. They notice that the numbers stay the same in related facts and recognize that part–total relationships are the reason. Students use what they know about part–total relationships to help them find unknowns in various positions.

title: Add or subtract to make groups equal.
objectives: Add or subtract to make groups equal.
i_can: I can add or subtract to make groups equal. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Through whole class and partner discussion, orally reason about how to make groups equal by adding or subtracting. Represent the change by writing a true number sentence.
key_questions: What are some ways to make two groups equal?
ad_texts: ["Add or subtract to make groups equal and write a true number sentence to match."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD6] Add or subtract to make groups equal and write a true number sentence to match.
laag: Students continue to deepen their understanding of the equal sign. They compare two groups of objects and make the groups equal by adding to or taking away from each group. Students represent the action by writing a true addition or subtraction number sentence.

title: Represent and solve compare with difference unknown problems, part 1.
objectives: Represent and solve compare with difference unknown problems, part 1.
i_can: I can find how many more. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model how many more comparison problems by using manipulatives and drawings. Orally describe a common error and identify how to correct it.
key_questions: What are different ways to find how many more?
ad_texts: ["Represent by using drawings and a number sentence and solve how many more word problems within 20."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD2] Represent by using drawings and a number sentence and solve how many more word problems within 20.
laag: Students compare sets of objects to figure out how many more are in one group than in another. They solve comparison problems concretely and pictorially. Students discuss two different representations of the same problem. One representation shows the “extra” amount in one group, and the other representation shows the “missing” amount that makes the groups equal. Students use addition and subtraction to show their thinking.

title: Represent and solve compare with difference unknown problems, part 2.
objectives: Represent and solve compare with difference unknown problems, part 2.
i_can: I can compare groups and then show how many more.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model how many more comparison problems by using labeled drawings, and orally explain solution strategies.
key_questions: What ways can we use to figure out how many more one group has than another?
ad_texts: ["Represent by using drawings and a number sentence and solve how many more word problems within 20."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD2] Represent by using drawings and a number sentence and solve how many more word problems within 20.
laag: Students consider a scenario in which two students buy a toy. With guidance from the teacher, students draw a picture to represent the situation and identify how many more dollars one child has than the other. Students then use the Read–Draw–Write process to solve a word problem that asks, How many more? They compare and discuss different representations.

title: Compare categories in a graph to figure out how many more.
objectives: Compare categories in a graph to figure out how many more.
i_can: I can compare groups on a graph. I can find the total and how many more.
language_objectives: Write to complete and label a graph that represents groups sorted by attributes, and write the total of each category. Orally explain how a graph is helpful for comparing groups.
key_questions: What makes a graph helpful for comparing groups?
ad_texts: ["Answer questions about a graph."]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD8] Answer questions about a graph.
laag: Students sort, organize, and then represent a set of objects in a graph. They ask and answer questions about the graph. Students focus on finding the total of all categories and use a comparison to find how many more are in one category than in another category.

title: Group to make ten when there are three parts.
objectives: Group to make ten when there are three parts.
i_can: I can group objects to make ten. I can add another part to find the total.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to group addends to make ten and justify why it is a helpful strategy.
key_questions: How can we use ten to make an easier problem?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD2] Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students learn to add three parts efficiently by grouping addends that make ten. Students apply the commutative and associative properties to their work as they think of addends in different orders and group them to make ten. This lesson introduces the term addend.

title: Make ten with three addends.
objectives: Make ten with three addends.
i_can: I can make ten. I can add another number to find the total.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model story problems by using drawings and labels. Orally explain how reordering addends helps to make ten.
key_questions: Why is it useful to think about ten when we add?
ad_texts: ["Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD1] Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)
laag: Students find the totals of three-addend equations by grouping two addends that make ten. They model the work with cubes and then use pictorial models to solve a word problem. Students explore how the Maya people wrote numbers, and they make connections between that notation and making ten.

title: Represent and solve three-addend word problems.
objectives: Represent and solve three-addend word problems.
i_can: I can make ten and then add a number to find the total. I can write a number sentence to match the story.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model three-addend story problems by using drawings and labels. Through whole class discussion and a partner game, orally evaluate whether two expressions that include a ten are equal and explain why.
key_questions: How can we make a problem with three addends easier?
ad_texts: ["Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD1] Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)
laag: Students use the make ten strategy to solve add to with result unknown word problems. They represent their thinking with drawings and number sentences. Students relate equivalent expressions to make true number sentences.

title: Use properties of addition to make three‑addend expressions easier.
objectives: Use properties of addition to make three‑addend expressions easier.
i_can: I can use what I know to group addends and find the total.
language_objectives: Orally describe ways to group addends to make an easier problem. Generalize that there are many ways to do so, even if the addends do not make ten.
key_questions: What are some ways to make an easier problem when addends are not partners to 10?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)", "Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD2] Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6) [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students write three-addend number sentences to represent pattern block puzzles. They discuss and practice grouping strategies for making the problem easier, even when two addends do not make ten.

title: Make ten when an addend is 5.
objectives: Make ten when an addend is 5.
i_can: I can break up a part to make ten. I can write a number sentence with three parts and find the total.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to break apart an addend to make ten when one of the addends is 5. Orally evaluate whether decomposing an addend to make ten is a helpful strategy and justify by using understanding of 10+ facts.
key_questions: How can we add to 5 efficiently?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students find the total of two-addend expressions by decomposing one addend into two parts to make ten with the other addend. They rewrite the expression as a number sentence to show how they decomposed the addend and found the total. Students use concrete and pictorial models to support their discussion.

title: Make ten when the first addend is 9.
objectives: Make ten when the first addend is 9.
i_can: I can break up a part to make ten. I can write a 3-part number sentence and find the total.
language_objectives: Describe orally, in writing, and by using manipulatives how to break apart an addend to make ten when the first addend is 9. Orally evaluate whether decomposing an addend to make ten is an efficient strategy and justify by using understanding of 10+ facts.
key_questions: How is it helpful to make ten with 9?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students watch and discuss a video that provides a natural context for making ten to add when the first addend is 9. They use a 10-frame and counters to model making ten by decomposing one addend to make ten and represent their thinking with a three-addend number sentence.

title: Make ten when the first addend is 8 or 9.
objectives: Make ten when the first addend is 8 or 9.
i_can: I can break up the second addend to make ten. I can show how I know and write a number sentence.
language_objectives: Describe orally, in writing, and by drawing how to break apart an addend to make ten when the first addend is 8 or 9. Orally evaluate whether breaking apart an addend to make ten is a helpful strategy and justify by using understanding of 10+ facts.
key_questions: Why is it helpful to make ten?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students use 5-group drawings to show ways to make ten to add when the first addend is 8 or 9. They represent their thinking about how to make ten in a variety of ways, including by rewriting two-addend expressions as three-addend expressions. Partners play a game to practice showing and explaining their thinking.

title: Make ten when the second addend is 8 or 9.
objectives: Make ten when the second addend is 8 or 9.
i_can: I can break up the first addend to make ten. I can draw how I know and write a number sentence.
language_objectives: Describe orally, in writing, and by drawing how to break apart an addend to make ten when the second addend is 8 or 9. Orally justify why breaking apart a smaller addend is an efficient way to make ten.
key_questions: Did you make ten with the first or second addend? Why?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students find the total when the second addend is 8 or 9. They show their thinking with drawings, number bonds, and number sentences. Students consider that some expressions may have other addends that are equally helpful for making ten. They play a game to continue practicing making easier problems.

title: Make ten with either addend.
objectives: Make ten with either addend.
i_can: I can break up either addend to make ten. I can show how I know and write a number sentence.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to break apart either addend to make ten and why that addend was chosen. Orally compare decomposing to add doubles and decomposing to make ten.
key_questions: Did you make ten with the first or second addend? Why?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: This lesson offers continued practice with the make ten strategy when both addends are close in value. Solving a word problem, engaging in a Whiteboard Exchange, and playing Bingo keep students engaged as they solidify their understanding of and ability to use the make ten strategy.

title: Make ten when there are three addends.
objectives: Make ten when there are three addends.
i_can: I can group or break up addends to make ten. I can tell how I know and write a number sentence.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to make ten when there are three addends and none of the addends are partners to ten. Orally explain why decomposing an addend to make an easier problem is a helpful strategy.
key_questions: What are ways to make an easier problem?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD2] Add within 20 with equations that have more than two addends. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students write three-addend number sentences to represent different images. They construct pattern blocks puzzles and represent them with three-addend expressions. Then students share and discuss various ways to make problems simpler when no two addends make ten. One of the ways is by decomposing an addend to make ten. There is no Problem Set in this lesson. This allows students to spend more time working with pattern block puzzles.

title: Represent and compare related situation equations, part 1.
objectives: Represent and compare related situation equations, part 1.
i_can: I can compare two stories. I can show how they have different addends and the same totals.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, retell, and model add to with result unknown story problems by using drawings, labels, and number paths. Evaluate orally and in writing whether two expressions are equal and explain why.
key_questions: Why can the total be the same when the number of addends is different?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod3.AD1] Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)
laag: Students write situation equations, or number sentences that describe the problem as written rather than the equation used to solve, to represent related add to with result unknown word problems. They show these number sentences on number paths, drawing hops to show each addend. Students compare the hops on number paths and reason about the equality of number sentences. This lesson prepares students to count on to get to ten by using a number path to add.

title: Represent and compare related situation equations, part 2.
objectives: Represent and compare related situation equations, part 2.
i_can: I can compare two stories by using number paths. I can show how they have different addends and the same totals.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model add to with result unknown and add to with change unknown story problems by using drawings, labels, and number paths. Orally compare addition strategies on a number path.
key_questions: Do you need the same number of parts to make the same total? Why?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod3.AD1] Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)
laag: Students represent and solve an add to with result unknown problem. Then they use their thinking to find the unknown part in an add to with change unknown problem. Students represent and compare the number sentences on a number path. This lesson continues to prepare students to count on to get to ten by using a number path to add.

title: Count on to make ten within 20.
objectives: Count on to make ten within 20.
i_can: I can show how I make ten with a number path.  I can write a 3-part number sentence.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to find an unknown addend by making a ten on a number path within 20. Orally compare making a ten on a number path with other math tools, such as drawings and number bonds.
key_questions: What stays the same about the make ten strategy, even when the tool changes?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students experiment with various ways to find an unknown addend by hopping on a floor-sized number path. As they experiment, they find that making ten is the most efficient strategy for finding unknown addends and totals. Through discussion, students confirm that they apply the same make ten strategy even when they choose different tools for solving.

title: Count on to make the next ten within 100.
objectives: Count on to make the next ten within 100.
i_can: I can show how I get to the next ten with a number path. I can write a number sentence.
language_objectives: Orally count by tens and ones between 0 and 120 to identify the next ten. Describe orally and in writing how to add by making the next ten on a number path, and explain why it is a helpful strategy.
key_questions: How can we use the make ten strategy to help us add larger numbers?
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD3] Add within 20 by using strategies such as applying the commutative and associative properties to make 10 or by counting on to 10. (1.OA.B.3, 1.OA.C.6)
laag: Students build a number path from 1 to 120. They use centimeter cubes to hop by tens from 10 to 120. Students play a game in which they hop in various ways: by ones, to the next ten, and to the next ten plus some more. This work sets up the number path as a linear model for making an easier problem by getting to the next ten. There is no Problem Set in this lesson.

title: Count and record a collection of objects.
objectives: Count and record a collection of objects.
i_can: I can group objects into tens. I can show how I count a group of objects.
language_objectives: Through listening and speaking, describe a strategy with a partner to estimate, count, and record a collection of objects. Write or draw to record how to organize and count a collection of objects. Include an estimate of a collection of objects and the actual number in the collection. Through listening and speaking, describe counting strategies, including making ten, to accurately count and compare and connect strategies.
key_questions: Does organizing objects into groups of 10 make it easier to find the total? How?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Represent a set of up to 50 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.a)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD7] Represent a set of up to 50 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.a)
laag: Partners organize, count, and record a collection of objects by using tools and strategies of their choice. Through comparing and connecting recordings of their work, students discuss the efficiency of making groups of 10 to count large collections. Students begin to see that ten objects can be represented as a group of 10. The term ten as a unit is introduced in this lesson. There is no Problem Set or Exit Ticket for this lesson. Instead, use the recording sheet to analyze student thinking after the lesson.

title: Identify ten as a unit.
objectives: Identify ten as a unit.
i_can: I can tell how many tens and ones are in a number. I can show groups of tens and ones.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model a story problem by using drawings and labels. Represent the value of each digit in a two-digit number orally and in writing. Orally distinguish between the units of a two-digit number (such as tens and ones).
key_questions: How does the way we write a number tell you about the tens and ones?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Represent a set of up to 50 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.a)", "Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD7] Represent a set of up to 50 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.a) [1.Mod3.AD8] Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)
laag: Students build and draw quantities, making groups of 10 and showing any leftover ones. They count by tens and then ones to find and write the total number. Students relate the digits in the number to their manipulatives and drawings to determine the value of each digit. The term unit is introduced in this lesson.

title: Add a two-digit number and a one-digit number.
objectives: Add a two-digit number and a one-digit number.
i_can: I can add the ones first. I can add the ten to find the total. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to break apart a two-digit number to show a basic addition fact, make an easier problem, and explain why it is a helpful strategy. Orally compare basic facts with two-digit plus one-digit addition equations.
key_questions: Why do we break up a number into tens and ones to add?
big_idea: Equal Expressions Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Add within 20 by decomposing a teen addend to add the ones first.", "Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD5] Add within 20 by decomposing a teen addend to add the ones first. [1.Mod3.AD8] Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)
laag: Students use place value concepts to find the total of a two-digit number and a one-digit number. They decompose the two-digit number into a ten and some ones, combine the ones with the one-digit addend, and add the total to the ten. Students find totals of related problems, such as 4 + 4 and 14 + 4, and discuss how the basic fact (4 + 4) can help them solve the other problem (14 + 4).

title: Subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number.
objectives: Subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number.
i_can: I can break a number into ten and some ones. I can take from the ones first and then add to 10.
language_objectives: Describe orally and in writing how to break apart a two-digit number to take from the ones first, and explain why it is a helpful strategy. Orally compare basic facts with two-digit minus one-digit subtraction equations.
key_questions: Why do we break up a number into tens and ones to subtract?
big_idea: Equal Expressions Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using tens and ones to take from the ones.", "Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD6] Subtract within 20 by using tens and ones to take from the ones. [1.Mod3.AD8] Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)
laag: Students use place value concepts to subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number. As in similar work with addition, students decompose the two-digit number into a ten and some ones. They subtract the one-digit subtrahend from the digit in the ones place and then add ten to find the difference.

title: Solve take from with change unknown problems with totals in the teens.
objectives: Solve take from with change unknown problems with totals in the teens.
i_can: I can solve word problems. I can show when I take from the ones or from ten.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model take from with change unknown story problems with totals in the teens by using drawings and labels. Orally justify when it makes sense to take away from the ones rather than the tens.
key_questions: When does it make sense to take away from the ones?
big_idea: Equal Expressions Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod3.AD8] Represent two-digit numbers within 50 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)
laag: Students use the Read–Draw–Write process to solve take from with change unknown word problems. This problem type requires students to find the subtrahend, or the subtracted part. Students draw to represent the total as a ten and some ones and then cross out to take away until they are left with the difference. Students reason about whether it makes sense to take away the unknown part from the ten or the ones.

title: Use strategies to subtract from a teen number.
objectives: Use strategies to subtract from a teen number.
i_can: I can subtract from a teen number. I can share my strategy.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model take from with result unknown story problems that have a teen number as the total. Listen to others share their solution strategies, including taking away in parts or all at once, in order to compare and connect solution strategies.
key_questions: What strategies can we use to make subtraction problems easier?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students solve a take from with result unknown problem that has a teen number as the total. They share the solution strategies taking from the ten and taking from the ones and the ten. Students apply these two strategies with cubes and explain how they made an easier problem. They contrast the efficiency of these strategies with counting back one by ones to subtract.

title: Take from ten to subtract from a teen number, part 1.
objectives: Take from ten to subtract from a teen number, part 1.
i_can: I can break the total into ten and some ones. I can take from ten.  I can add what is left.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model take from with result unknown story problems that have a teen number as the total. Describe orally and in writing how to take from ten to subtract, and orally explain why this is an efficient strategy.
key_questions: What makes taking from ten efficient?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students focus on the take from ten strategy. They show the total as a ten and some ones, both by drawing 5-groups and by using cubes. Then they take 8 or 9 all at once from ten and add the remaining parts. The teacher records students’ thinking with more abstract number bonds and number sentences.

title: Take from ten to subtract from a teen number, part 2.
objectives: Take from ten to subtract from a teen number, part 2.
i_can: I can choose a tool to take from ten. I can add what is left.  I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model take from with result unknown story problems that have a teen number as the total. Describe orally and in writing how to subtract by taking from ten all at once, and evaluate which tool is most helpful.
key_questions: Which tool is most helpful when taking from ten? Why?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students continue to take from ten by using a variety of tools such as hands, cubes, and 5-group row drawings. Students record their thinking with number bonds and discuss the take from ten strategy as well as which tools they can use to carry out this strategy. • Copy or print the 5-Group

title: Subtract by counting on.
objectives: Subtract by counting on.
i_can: I can count on to find the unknown part. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to subtract by counting on from the known part to the total. Orally compare counting on to find an unknown part with taking from ten.
key_questions: How can we count on to solve a subtraction problem?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students analyze a drawing of the take from ten strategy to see the part–part–total relationship. Recognizing this relationship helps students connect subtraction to the strategy of counting on to find an unknown part. They use a number path to solve subtraction problems by counting on.

title: Decompose the subtrahend to count back.
objectives: Decompose the subtrahend to count back.
i_can: I can subtract by breaking up a part and counting back to ten. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Describe orally and through actions how to subtract by breaking a subtrahend into two parts, counting back to ten, and then counting back the rest. Orally explain why counting back to ten is a helpful strategy.
key_questions: Why do we use ten when we count back to subtract?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students subtract by breaking the subtrahend into two parts. They count back the first part to get to ten, and then they count back the rest. Students represent their thinking on a number path and with cubes. They learn a way to record their thinking by using numbers and arrows.

title: Choose a strategy to make an easier problem.
objectives: Choose a strategy to make an easier problem.
i_can: I can choose my strategy to subtract. I can show how I subtract.
language_objectives: Orally justify how a self-selected strategy is the best choice to find the difference of a given subtraction problem.
key_questions: What strategies can we use to make subtraction problems easier?
ad_texts: ["Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10."]
ad_full: [1.Mod3.AD4] Subtract within 20 by using strategies such as counting on to 10, counting back to 10, or taking from 10.
laag: Students discuss a series of subtraction problems, intentionally selecting strategies for solving each. They take time to make sense of each problem and self-select a subtraction strategy to make the problem easier (take from ten, count on, or count back using ten). Students also self-select tools to show their thinking, such as drawings or number paths.

title: Pose and solve varied word problems.
objectives: Pose and solve varied word problems.
i_can: I can ask math questions and solve word problems. I can share my strategy.
language_objectives: Read, listen to, and model add to with result unknown, compare, and take from with result unknown story problems. Through listening and speaking, describe solution strategies and compare and connect them. Orally describe how asking meta-cognitive questions can help to self-monitor when solving problems.
key_questions: What did we learn about asking math questions? What did we learn about answering math questions (solving problems)?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types.", "Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod2.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 involving grades K and 1 addition and subtraction problem types. [1.Mod3.AD1] Represent word problems by using drawings and a number sentence and solve word problems within 20 involving three addends. (1.OA.A.2, 1.OA.B.3)
laag: Students watch a video and generate questions about the context, differentiating mathematical questions from non-math ones. Then they solve three real-world word problem types—add to with result unknown, compare, and take from with result unknown—self-selecting strategies and tools to represent and solve them. Students experience and work through productive struggle. After each question type, students share and discuss their work. There is no Problem Set in this lesson.

title: Compare and order objects by length.
objectives: Compare and order objects by length.
i_can: I can compare objects. I can put them in order by length.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to order objects by length. Orally compare the lengths of objects in an ordered set by using comparative statements that include the words shorter, taller, shortest, and tallest.
key_questions: What strategies can we use to compare objects and order them by length?
ad_texts: ["Order three objects by length by using direct comparison."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD4] Order three objects by length by using direct comparison.
laag: Students reason about and compare heights using terms such as shorter, taller, shortest, and tallest. They reason about the importance of aligning endpoints of objects when comparing them. Students work in pairs to order a collection of classroom objects from shortest to longest. They make comparative statements about the objects.

title: Reason to order and compare heights.
objectives: Reason to order and compare heights.
i_can: I can compare objects to put objects in order. I can tell how I know.
language_objectives: Listen to comparative statements to order a set of objects by height. Orally justify how objects are ordered by using the words shorter, taller, shortest, and tallest.
key_questions: How can we use information about which objects are shorter or taller to put them in order?
ad_texts: ["Order three objects by length by using direct comparison."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD4] Order three objects by length by using direct comparison.
laag: Students order a set of owls according to their height. Rather than compare owls directly, students listen to clues about the owls’ heights. They reason about the clues to put the owls in the correct order. Students make comparison statements about the ordered owls and explain their thinking. Extra time is allotted for the Problem Set so students can cut out and order the objects.

title: Compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
objectives: Compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
i_can: I can use one other object to compare two different objects that are not next to each other.
language_objectives: Conjecture ways to compare objects that are not next to each other. Read sentence frames to summarize the process of indirectly comparing the length of objects. Orally and in writing, compare the lengths of three objects by using the words shorter, shortest, taller, tallest, and longer.
key_questions: How can we compare two objects that we can’t put next to each other by using a third object?
ad_texts: ["Compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD5] Compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
laag: Students reason about ways to indirectly compare the lengths of objects. Students are presented with pictures of animals that cannot be lined up or placed side by side for direct comparison. Instead, students use a third object, such as a tree, plate, or stick, to indirectly compare the lengths of the animals. This concept is called transitivity.

title: Measure accurately with centimeter cubes.
objectives: Measure accurately with centimeter cubes.
i_can: I can use centimeter cubes to measure objects. I can write the total.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to measure the length of an object accurately by using centimeter cubes, and state the total length in centimeters. Evaluate ways to measure the lengths of objects, and orally summarize productive measuring behaviors.
key_questions: How do we use tools to measure the length of an object?
ad_texts: ["Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD7] Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters.
laag: Students use centimeter cubes to measure length. They practice using behaviors that help them measure accurately, such as using endpoints, putting cubes in a straight line, and placing them with no gaps or overlaps. The terms length and measure are introduced in this lesson.

title: Measure and compare lengths.
objectives: Measure and compare lengths.
i_can: I can measure length to compare two objects. I can use a number sentence to show the comparison.
language_objectives: Orally compare the lengths of objects by using numerical measurements and the words shorter, longer, greater than, less than, and equal to. Orally analyze number sentences that include the symbols <, >, and =, and relate the numbers to lengths.
key_questions: How can we compare objects and record our thinking?
big_idea: Measuring with Objects Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Measure and compare the lengths of two objects. (1.NBT.B.3, 1.MD.A.1, 1.MD.A.2)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD3] Measure and compare the lengths of two objects. (1.NBT.B.3, 1.MD.A.1, 1.MD.A.2)
laag: Students measure pairs of objects in order to compare them. Rather than using direct comparison, students use numerical lengths to determine which object is longer or shorter. Students record their thinking by writing number sentences that use the symbols >, =, and <.

title: Measure and order lengths.
objectives: Measure and order lengths.
i_can: I can measure objects. I can compare objects and put them in order.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to order a group of objects by length by using numerical measurements. Orally compare lengths and order objects by using numerical measurements and the words shorter, shortest, longer, longest, taller, and tallest.
key_questions: How can we order objects by length when we cannot line them up together?
ad_texts: ["Measure and order the lengths of three or more objects. (1.MD.A.1, 1.MD.A.2)"]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD6] Measure and order the lengths of three or more objects. (1.MD.A.1, 1.MD.A.2)
laag: Students order objects that are of similar length but cannot be compared directly. Students measure the objects and then use their measurements to put the objects in ascending and descending order. Students compare objects within the ordered set and write comparison number sentences to record their thinking.

title: Use 10-centimeter sticks and centimeter cubes to measure.
objectives: Use 10-centimeter sticks and centimeter cubes to measure.
i_can: I can measure with a 10-centimeter stick and centimeter cubes. I can write the lengths.
language_objectives: Orally justify why measuring lengths greater than 10 centimeters by using a 10-centimeter stick is more efficient than using centimeter cubes.
key_questions: How does using a 10-centimeter stick as a tool help us to measure objects?
ad_texts: ["Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD7] Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters.
laag: • The Unknown Addend Fluency Sheets and Students estimate a distance and then measure it two ways. First, they Frog Jump must be torn out of student measure it with centimeter cubes, and then with 10-centimeter sticks and some books. Consider whether to prepare these centimeter cubes. title: Compare to find how much longer.
objectives: Compare to find how much longer.
i_can: I can compare to find how much longer one object is than another. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally compare the measurements of two objects by using the words longer and shorter and justify by relating place value units to measuring tools. Orally describe how to find the difference in lengths between two objects.
key_questions: How can we tell how much longer one object is than another?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths.", "Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths. [1.Mod4.AD7] Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters.
laag: Students measure pairs of caterpillars by using 10-centimeter sticks and cubes. Then they compare the parallel representations of the measurements and consider ways to see the difference, or how much longer one is than the other. Students also represent the lengths and difference with a drawing and a number sentence.

title: Compare to find how much shorter.
objectives: Compare to find how much shorter.
i_can: I can compare to find how much shorter one object is than another.  I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to find the difference in lengths between two objects. Orally generalize about why the difference is the same when comparing two objects and asking how much longer or shorter one is than the other.
key_questions: Why is the answer the same when we compare objects and ask how much longer or how much shorter one object is than a second object?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths.", "Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths. [1.Mod4.AD7] Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters.
laag: Students measure and compare different objects. They use their comparisons to relate finding how much longer one object is than a second object to finding how much shorter the second object is than the first object. By using the same context and representations to answer both questions, they discover that the solution pathways are similar and the answer to both questions is the same.

title: Find the unknown longer length.
objectives: Find the unknown longer length.
i_can: I can use one objects length and add cubes to find another objects length. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to use a known length to find an unknown longer length. Orally describe how a number sentence matches the objects and shows the difference in their lengths.
key_questions: When we know one length, how do we find a second length?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths.
laag: Students use information they are given about the relationship between two lengths to find one length that is unknown. They use 10-centimeter sticks and cubes to measure or represent the known length. To find the unknown length, they represent the known length, reason about its relationship to the unknown length, and add more.

title: Find the unknown shorter length.
objectives: Find the unknown shorter length.
i_can: I can use one objects length and take away cubes to find another objects length. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to use a known length to find an unknown shorter length. Orally describe how a number sentence matches objects and shows the difference in their lengths.
key_questions: When we know one length, how do we find a second length?
ad_texts: ["Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD1] Represent and solve word problems within 20 in grade 1 addition and subtraction comparison problem types involving represented lengths.
laag: Students continue to use information they are given about the relationship between two lengths to find one length that is unknown. In lesson 12, they found the longer length. In this lesson, they find the shorter length. To find the unknown length, they represent the known length a second time, reason about its relationship to the unknown length, and take away.

title: Measure to find patterns.
objectives: Measure to find patterns.
i_can: I can use patterns to help me know the height of the next object.  I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally generalize about how finding patterns helps determine the height of the next object without measuring it.
key_questions: How do patterns help us figure out the height of the next object without measuring it?
ad_texts: ["Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters."]
ad_full: [1.Mod4.AD7] Measure the length of an object and write the length as a whole number of centimeters.
laag: Students build a series of pattern block towers. They measure each tower and notice a pattern: Each tower is 2 centimeters taller than the previous tower. They analyze other sets of towers to find shrinking patterns. Students use the patterns to predict the height of the next object.

title: Tell time to the hour and half hour by using digital and analog clocks.
objectives: Tell time to the hour and half hour by using digital and analog clocks.
i_can: I can tell time to the hour and the half hour on different kinds of clocks.  I can show how I know.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally justify why times in writing match times presented on a clock by using terms such as hour and minutes.
key_questions: What time is it? How do you know?
ad_texts: ["Tell time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks."]
ad_full: [1.Mod5.AD10] Tell time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
laag: Students analyze an analog clock and a digital clock that show the same time. They learn how each clock represents the hour and minutes and practice reading the time to the hour and half hour on both kinds of clocks.

title: Count a collection and record the total in units of tens and ones.

language_objectives: Through listening and speaking, identify the value of each digit in a two-digit number by using the terms value, digit, ones place, and tens place.
key_questions: What is the value of each digit in a two-digit number? How do you know?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Represent a set of up to 99 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2.a)", "Determine the values represented by the digits of a two-digit number."]
ad_full: [1.Mod5.AD1] Represent a set of up to 99 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2.a) [1.Mod5.AD3] Determine the values represented by the digits of a two-digit number.

title: Represent a number in multiple ways by trading 10 ones for a ten.
objectives: Represent a number in multiple ways by trading 10 ones for a ten.
i_can: I can trade 10 ones for a ten. I can use tens and ones to show different ways to make a total.
language_objectives: Orally explain how to compose 10 ones and trade for a ten. Read and write to show a two-digit number in different ways by using a place value chart and a drawing.
key_questions: How can we represent the same number in different ways using tens and ones?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
ad_texts: ["Represent two-digit numbers within 99 as tens and ones. (1.NBT.B.2, 1.NBT.B.2.b, 1.NBT.B.2.c)", "Determine the values represented by the digits of a two-digit number."]

They discuss the equivalence of various ways they can represent a given total.

title: Reason about equivalent representations of a number.
objectives: Reason about equivalent representations of a number.
i_can: I can show the same total in different ways. I can show how I know.

key_questions: Why can different representations show the same total?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones

ad_full: [1.Mod5.AD1] Represent a set of up to 99 objects with a two-digit number by composing tens. (1.NBT.A.1, 1.NBT.B.2.a) [1.Mod5.AD2] Represent two-digit numbers within 99 as tens and ones. title: Add 10 or take 10 from a two-digit number.
objectives: Add 10 or take 10 from a two-digit number.
i_can: I can tell what is 10 more or 10 less than a number. I can show how I know.
language_objectives: Orally count forward or backward by tens to find 10 more or 10 less than a given number. Orally analyze sequences of digits to describe and extend number patterns by using place value language and the terms digits and value.
key_questions: What do you notice about the digit in the tens place when you add 10 to a number? What do you notice about the digit in the tens place when you take 10 from a number?
ad_texts: ["Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number."]
ad_full: [1.Mod5.AD9] Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number.
laag: Students count forward and backward by tens. They look at recordings of the counts and notice a pattern in the digits in the tens place. They study the pattern further by using concrete materials to add 10 to a number or take 10 from the number. In one activity, students watch a video and model the actions of adding and taking 10. There is no Problem Set in this lesson. This allows students to spend more time working with concrete manipulatives.

title: Use place value reasoning to compare two quantities.
objectives: Use place value reasoning to compare two quantities.
i_can: I can use tens and ones to compare numbers. I can show which number is greater or less.
language_objectives: Listen to and then build on the reasoning of others. Orally justify the comparison of two quantities.
key_questions: How can we compare two totals?
big_idea: Reasoning About Equality Tens and Ones
