ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD3] Write a repeated addition equation to represent an array, including writing an equation to express an even number as the sum of two equal addends. (2.OA.C.3, 2.OA.C.4) [2.Mod6.AD5] Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares.
laag: Students decompose two same-size arrays differently. They find all possible ways to make an array by using 16 square tiles and 24 square tiles. They conclude that arrays can look different but still have the same total.

title: Decompose an array and relate it to a number bond.
objectives: Decompose an array and relate it to a number bond.
i_can: I can decompose an array and represent parts with a number bond and repeated addition sentence.
language_objectives: Listen to and follow directions involving rows or columns as the unit to identify smaller arrays within larger arrays. Orally explain how larger arrays can be decomposed into smaller parts and orally relate this to decomposing a number.
key_questions: How does an array show us that larger units are made up of smaller units? How is composing and decomposing an array similar to or different from decomposing a number?
big_idea: Skip Counting to 100 Seeing Fractions in Shapes Squares in an Array
ad_texts: ["Write a repeated addition equation to represent an array, including writing an equation to express an even number as the sum of two equal addends. (2.OA.C.3, 2.OA.C.4)", "Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares."]
ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD3] Write a repeated addition equation to represent an array, including writing an equation to express an even number as the sum of two equal addends. (2.OA.C.3, 2.OA.C.4) [2.Mod6.AD5] Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares.
laag: Students shade a smaller array within a larger array and use a number bond and a repeated addition sentence to represent the array. They recognize that a row or a column can be considered an equal group, or unit.

title: Relate doubles to even numbers and write equations to express the sums.
objectives: Relate doubles to even numbers and write equations to express the sums.
i_can: I can explain what makes a number even.
language_objectives: Orally analyze numbers and justify whether they are even by skip-counting, recalling doubles facts, and examining equal-length tile arrangements. Through listening to and participating in a class discussion, orally generalize that the sums of all doubles facts are even numbers.
key_questions: How do you know if a number is even?
ad_texts: ["Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd.", "Skip-count by twos."]
ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD2] Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd. [2.Mod6.AD6] Skip-count by twos.
laag: Students discover that when any number from 1 to 10 is doubled, the resulting number is even and that any even number can be written as a doubles fact. They arrange doubles into rectangular arrays (e.g., 2 rows of 7, or 2 sevens) and write an equation to show the total as a sum of two equal addends (e.g., 7 + 7 = 14). This lesson formalizes the term even number.

title: Pair objects and skip-count to determine whether a number is even or odd.
objectives: Pair objects and skip-count to determine whether a number is even or odd.
i_can: I can use strategies to tell whether a number is even or odd.
language_objectives: Orally analyze numeric and pictorial sequences to identify patterns and predict what comes next. Write an explanation of whether a number is even or odd and justify reasoning.
key_questions: What happens to an even number when 1 is added or subtracted? How do you determine whether a number is even or odd?
big_idea: Skip Counting to 100 Squares in an Array
ad_texts: ["Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd."]
ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD2] Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd.
laag: Students form pairs to determine that even numbers must have a partner. Then students build arrays to model each number from 2 to 20. In doing so, students determine that they can write even numbers as a doubles fact and that the last digit in an even number is always 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8. This lesson formalizes the term odd number.

title: Use rectangular arrays to investigate combinations of even and odd numbers.
objectives: Use rectangular arrays to investigate combinations of even and odd numbers.
i_can: I can use patterns to tell which combinations of even and odd numbers make an even sum and which make an odd sum.
language_objectives: Orally analyze patterns to predict whether larger numbers are even or odd. Orally construct viable arguments by using a sentence frame to justify whether a number is even or odd.
key_questions: What types of numbers, even or odd, can you use to compose an even number? What types of numbers, even or odd, can you use to compose an odd number?
big_idea: Skip Counting to 100 Squares in an Array
ad_texts: ["Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd."]
ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD2] Determine whether the number of objects in a group (up to 20) is even or odd.
laag: Students use rectangular arrays to investigate what happens when they add two even numbers, an even number and an odd number, and two odd numbers. Students determine whether the sum is even or odd, and they apply the pattern to larger numbers.

title: Solve word problems that involve equal groups and arrays.
objectives: Solve word problems that involve equal groups and arrays.
i_can: I can solve word problems that have equal groups.
language_objectives: Read and solve word problems involving equal groups and arrays. Listen to and orally describe the problems’ meanings and possible strategies for solving them. Orally compare and connect solution strategies. Write to explain whether the total is an even or odd number.
key_questions: Can we represent a word problem in different ways? Why?

ad_full: [2.Mod6.AD1] Represent and solve word problems involving equal groups by using manipulatives and drawings. laag: Students draw pictorial models to solve word problems that involve equal groups and arrays. They articulate how each part of the model represents the problem. They transition from using a pictorial model to a more abstract model, the tape diagram. Students connect the pictorial and abstract models as they share their solution strategies.

title: Use various strategies to fluently add and subtract within 100 and know all sums and differences within 20 from memory.
objectives: Use various strategies to fluently add and subtract within 100 and know all sums and differences within 20 from memory.
i_can: I can fluently add and subtract within 100.
language_objectives: Read questions and answer them in writing to reflect on and evaluate progress toward fluency with addition and subtraction. Listen to and follow directions and orally engage with a partner in a variety of fluency games.
key_questions: Which addition facts within 20 do I know from memory? Which facts do I still need to practice? Which addition and subtraction strategies work best for me? Which strategies have I not mastered yet?
ad_texts: ["This lesson serves as a culminating activity and formative assessment of the required grade 2 fluencies. Its content is not, therefore, included on summative assessments in module 6."]
ad_full: This lesson serves as a culminating activity and formative assessment of the required grade 2 fluencies. Its content is not, therefore, included on summative assessments in module 6.
laag: Students engage in activities that focus on fluently adding and subtracting within 100 by using various strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction. Students also demonstrate their ability to know all sums and differences within 20 from memory. There is no Fluency or Problem Set for this lesson. The Exit Ticket provides students with an opportunity to reflect on their learning.

title: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
objectives: Organize, count, and represent a collection of objects.
i_can: I can count a collection and explain the ways I organize and count.
language_objectives: Write or draw to record how to organize and count a collection of objects. Include an estimate of the number of objects, the actual number of objects in the collection, and an equation to describe how to find the total. Listen to and orally describe counting strategies—including counting by ones, skip-counting, and recognizing a total—to accurately count. Orally compare and connect strategies. In writing, explain the choice of units used to count the collection and the way that counting by units helps to find the total.
key_questions: How can we use groups to help us organize?
ad_texts: ["This lesson is foundational to the work of grade 3 and builds from 2.NBT.A.2. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in grade 3."]
ad_full: This lesson is foundational to the work of grade 3 and builds from 2.NBT.A.2. Its content is intended to serve as a formative assessment and is therefore not included on summative assessments in grade 3.
laag: This student-driven lesson provides an opportunity to gather formative assessment data as students work with counting collections. Students decide how to organize, count, and represent the items. They analyze the work of others and discuss efficient strategies as a class. There is no Problem Set for this lesson. Instead, use classroom observations and student work to analyze student thinking after the lesson. The Exit Ticket for this lesson serves as an opportunity for students to reflect on their counting strategies.

title: Interpret equal groups as multiplication.
objectives: Interpret equal groups as multiplication.
i_can: I can represent equal groups with a multiplication equation.
language_objectives: Listen to and orally discuss various ways to describe equal groups by using the terms repeated addition, unit form, and multiplication. Orally determine a total by using skip-counting.
key_questions: How is writing a multiplication equation more efficient than writing a repeated addition equation? What is the relationship between equal groups, repeated addition, unit form, and multiplication equations?
big_idea: Number Flexibility to for All Four Operations
ad_texts: ["Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication."]
ad_full: [3.Mod1.AD1] Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication.
laag: Students find the total of equal groups using skip-counting and repeated addition. Students describe the groups in unit form and write related multiplication equations. This lesson formalizes the terms multiply and multiplication and introduces the multiplication symbol,

title: Relate multiplication to the array model.
objectives: Relate multiplication to the array model.
i_can: I can use an array to represent equal groups and write a multiplication equation to find the total.
language_objectives: Orally explain how arrays relate to equal groups and multiplication equations. Orally identify the product in a multiplication equation.
key_questions: How does an array show equal groups? How does an array show each number in a multiplication equation?
big_idea: Number Flexibility to for All Four Operations
ad_texts: ["Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication."]
ad_full: [3.Mod1.AD1] Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication.
laag: Students build concrete arrays of fives and tens and relate them to equal groups, unit form, and multiplication to find the total. They relate the concrete array to a rekenrek and draw tape diagrams to represent equal groups. This lesson formalizes the term product.

title: Interpret the meaning of factors as number of groups or number in each group.
objectives: Interpret the meaning of factors as number of groups or number in each group.
i_can: I can describe what the factors in a multiplication expression represent.
language_objectives: Orally explain how the number of groups, the number in each group, and the total are each represented in equal groups, arrays, tape diagrams, and equations by using the terms factors and product.
key_questions: What do the factors represent in multiplication equations? How can the same multiplication equation represent an equal group picture and an array?
big_idea: Number Flexibility to for All Four Operations
ad_texts: ["Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication."]
ad_full: [3.Mod1.AD1] Represent a multiplication situation with a model and convert between several representations of multiplication.
laag: Students relate equal groups, arrays, and tape diagrams to multiplication equations. They interpret the meaning of factors in equations as either the number of groups or the number in each group. This lesson introduces the term factor.

title: Represent and solve multiplication word problems by using drawings and equations.
objectives: Represent and solve multiplication word problems by using drawings and equations.
i_can: I can solve multiplication word problems.
language_objectives: Read word problems involving multiplication. Write or draw to record a solution strategy and an equation to solve a word problem involving multiplication. Listen to and orally describe solution strategies and representations—including equal groups, arrays, and tape diagrams—to find the product and compare and connect solution strategies
key_questions: How is a tape diagram a useful model to use when solving multiplication word problems? How do you decide which model to use when solving a multiplication word problem?
big_idea: Number Flexibility to for All Four Operations
ad_texts: ["Solve one-step word problems by using multiplication and division within involving factors and divisors and"]
ad_full: [3.Mod1.AD3] Solve one-step word problems by using multiplication and division within involving factors and divisors and
laag: Students select strategies to represent and solve multiplication word problems by using drawings and equations. A video provides context for the word problems. After working independently to solve the problems, students share their work to compare and connect various representations and strategies.

title: Explore measurement and partitive division by modeling concretely and drawing.
objectives: Explore measurement and partitive division by modeling concretely and drawing.
i_can: I can represent equal sharing by using the number of groups and the number in each group.
language_objectives: Orally explain what each number represents in both measurement and partitive division situations by using the terms total, number of equal groups, and number in each group. Read division situations and orally describe to a partner how solution strategies change based on whether the number of equal groups or the number in each group is known.
key_questions: How can equal sharing be done in different ways? Why is it helpful to think about what the numbers in an equal-sharing problem represent?
big_idea: Number Flexibility to for All Four Operations
ad_texts: ["Represent a division situation with a model and convert between several representations of division."]
ad_full: [3.Mod1.AD2] Represent a division situation with a model and convert between several representations of division.

title: Subtract a fraction from a mixed number, part 1.

title: Subtract a fraction from a mixed number, part 2.
objectives: Subtract a fraction from a mixed number, part 2.

title: Subtract a mixed number from a mixed number.
objectives: Subtract a mixed number from a mixed number.

language_objectives: With a partner, orally discuss how to represent mixed numbers in different ways: with place value disks, on number lines, and by using decimal, fraction, and unit form. With a partner, orally analyze and describe the symmetry of the place value units on a place value chart.
key_questions: How can we use what we know about mixed numbers to represent ones, tenths, and hundredths in decimal form? What are the similarities among the place value units of hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, and hundredths?

ad_full: [4.Mod5.AD1] Express fractions with denominator as equivalent fractions with denominator (4.NF.C.5) tenths and [4.Mod5.AD3] Represent hundredths in decimal form, fraction form, or by using a model.
laag: Students use place value disks and number lines to represent numbers that include the fractional unit of hundredths. They represent the numbers as mixed numbers and in decimal form. Students extend their understanding of the place value chart to include the units of tenths and hundredths.

title: Represent decimal numbers in expanded form.
objectives: Represent decimal numbers in expanded form.
i_can: I can write decimal numbers in expanded form.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally compare different representations of expanded form—unit form, decimal form, and fraction form—for the same decimal number.
key_questions: In what different ways can we represent decimal numbers in expanded form?
ad_texts: ["Express fractions with denominator as equivalent fractions with denominator (4.NF.C.5) tenths and", "Represent hundredths in decimal form, fraction form, or by using a model."]
ad_full: [4.Mod5.AD1] Express fractions with denominator as equivalent fractions with denominator (4.NF.C.5) tenths and [4.Mod5.AD3] Represent hundredths in decimal form, fraction form, or by using a model.
laag: Students represent decimal numbers with place value disks and then express the amounts in expanded form. They record expanded form with numbers written in unit form, decimal form, and fraction form. Students are given numbers on place value cards or on a place value chart and express the numbers in expanded form.

title: Compare measurements expressed as decimal numbers.
objectives: Compare measurements expressed as decimal numbers.
i_can: I can compare measurements expressed in decimal form.
language_objectives: Write or draw to record comparing up to three measurements written as decimal numbers, and orally justify the comparisons. Listen to and orally describe various representations to compare decimal numbers and compare and connect solution strategies.
key_questions: What strategies for comparing whole numbers and fractions can be used to compare decimal numbers?
big_idea: Visual Fraction Models Circles, Fractions, and Decimals
ad_texts: ["two decimal", "Compare numbers to hundredths and justify the conclusions."]
ad_full: two decimal [4.Mod5.AD4] Compare numbers to hundredths and justify the conclusions.
laag: Students compare measurements expressed as decimal numbers. Pictures and models support students as they use what they know about comparing whole numbers and fractions to select a strategy to compare decimal numbers. Students use words and symbols to make comparison statements.

title: Use pictorial representations to compare decimal numbers.
objectives: Use pictorial representations to compare decimal numbers.
i_can: I can use pictures and number lines to compare decimal numbers.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, compare decimal numbers by using the phrases greater than, equal to, or less than and the symbols or Justify the comparisons orally by referencing a model or by using place value language.
key_questions: In what ways can we use place value units when comparing decimal numbers?

ad_full: two decimal [4.Mod5.AD4] Compare numbers to hundredths and justify the conclusions.
laag: Students represent and compare decimal numbers by shading area models and by using place value disks. title: Compare and order decimal numbers.
objectives: Compare and order decimal numbers.
i_can: I can compare and order decimal numbers.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, compare and order decimal numbers. Justify the comparisons orally by using place value language. Read word problems involving decimal numbers. Orally compare the decimal numbers and justify the comparisons by using the context of the word problem and place value understanding.
key_questions: How can we use what we know about fractions and decimal numbers to help us order decimal numbers?
big_idea: Visual Fraction Models Circles, Fractions, and Decimals
ad_texts: ["two decimal", "Compare numbers to hundredths and justify the conclusions. ( 4 . N F . C .7)"]
ad_full: two decimal [4.Mod5.AD4] Compare numbers to hundredths and justify the conclusions. ( 4 . N F . C .7)
laag: Students use what they know about ordering fractions to order decimal fractions and decimal numbers. They order the fractions and numbers from least to greatest and from greatest to least. They compare money and compare measurement units in context. Students apply their new learning of comparison and ordering of decimal numbers to complete a variety of comparison tasks with an emphasis on mental math strategies.

title: Apply fraction equivalence to add tenths and hundredths.
objectives: Apply fraction equivalence to add tenths and hundredths.
i_can: I can add tenths and hundredths.
language_objectives: Write or draw to record how to add decimal fractions with tenths to decimal fractions with hundredths. Listen to and orally discuss solution strategies to find the sum of decimal fractions— including using area models, number lines, multiplication and unit form, and breaking apart an addend—and compare and connect solution strategies.
key_questions: Why are equivalent fractions important when we add tenths and hundredths?
ad_texts: ["two fractions with", "Add respective denominators and"]
ad_full: two fractions with [4.Mod5.AD2] Add respective denominators and
laag: Students use what they know about equivalent fractions and the addition of fractions with like units to add decimal fractions of tenths and hundredths. Students express tenths as an equivalent amount of hundredths and represent the addition with select strategies. They examine different strategies and compare them to their own strategy. Students reason about the efficiency of their chosen strategy.

title: Apply fraction equivalence to add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths.
objectives: Apply fraction equivalence to add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths.
i_can: I can add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths.
language_objectives: Orally compare solution strategies for finding the sum of mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths. Orally explain and justify the method chosen to add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths.
key_questions: How can we use prior learning to add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths?
ad_texts: ["two fractions with", "Add respective denominators and"]
ad_full: two fractions with [4.Mod5.AD2] Add respective denominators and
laag: Students use what they know about equivalent fractions and the addition of mixed numbers with like units to add mixed numbers with tenths and hundredths. Students express tenths as an equivalent amount of hundredths and represent their addition with different methods. They discuss the similarities and differences between methods.

title: Solve word problems with tenths and hundredths.
objectives: Solve word problems with tenths and hundredths.
i_can: I can add tenths and hundredths to solve word problems.
language_objectives: Read word problems involving addition of decimal numbers with tenths and hundredths. Write or draw to record a solution strategy and an equation to solve the problem. Listen to and orally discuss models and solution strategies for finding a sum—including using the arrow way and adding like units to make compare and connect solution strategies.
key_questions: How can we use what we know about adding fractions to solve word problems with decimal numbers? Why is it important to assess the reasonableness of our answers when solving word problems?
big_idea: Fraction Flexibility Circles, Fractions, and Decimals
ad_texts: ["Add two fractions with respective denominators and (4.NF.C.5) word problems", "Solve involving addition of decimal numbers."]
ad_full: [4.Mod5.AD2] Add two fractions with respective denominators and (4.NF.C.5) word problems [4.Mod5.AD5] Solve involving addition of decimal numbers.
laag: Students examine sample work that shows the addition of decimal numbers by writing the decimal numbers as fractions before adding. Students select their own strategies to represent and solve one-step addition word problems with decimal numbers. After working independently to solve the problems, students share their work to compare and connect various methods. Students also assess the reasonableness of their answers by using what they know about decimal numbers and their relationship to whole numbers.

title: Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles.
objectives: Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles.
i_can: I can draw and name figures.
language_objectives: Use terms such as figure, point, endpoint, line segment, line, ray, angle, and construct to orally describe and name figures. Listen to draw a figure based on a partner’s description.
key_questions: Why do we mark points with dots and draw lines? How are line segments, lines, and rays similar and different? How are angles formed?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students draw points, lines, line segments, rays, and angles. They identify these in familiar mathematical and real-world figures and use appropriate notation. This lesson formalizes the terms figure, point, endpoint, line segment, line, ray, and angle and introduces the term construct.

title: Identify right, acute, obtuse, and straight angles.
objectives: Identify right, acute, obtuse, and straight angles.
i_can: I can classify angles based on their size.
language_objectives: Use terms such as classify, vertex, arc, right angle, acute angle, obtuse angle, and straight angle to orally describe and name angles.
key_questions: How can you identify right, acute, obtuse, and straight angles?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students make a right-angle tool to identify different types of angles in real-world and mathematical figures. They use the right-angle tool to describe angles as right, acute, or obtuse in relation to the right angle of the tool, and they describe a straight angle. This lesson formalizes the terms classify, vertex, acute angle, obtuse angle, and straight angle.

title: Draw right, acute, obtuse, and straight angles.
objectives: Draw right, acute, obtuse, and straight angles.
i_can: I can draw different types of angles.
language_objectives: Orally justify why given statements about angles are always, sometimes, or never true. Use terms such as vertex, arc, right angle, acute angle, obtuse angle, and straight angle to orally compare and classify angles. Justify the classifications orally and in writing.
key_questions: What tools are helpful for drawing angles? What should a drawing of an angle include?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students draw angles using a straightedge and a right-angle tool. They reason about how to draw an angle when a single ray is given and how to draw an angle from a description. Students name the angles in different ways, classify the angles by their size, and notice that angles can have rays drawn with different lengths and can be oriented on the page in various ways.

title: Identify, define, and draw perpendicular lines.
objectives: Identify, define, and draw perpendicular lines.
i_can: I can name and draw lines that form a right angle.
language_objectives: Write statements to identify and name two perpendicular lines, rays, or line segments by using the perpendicular symbol. Use terms such as perpendicular line, line, line segment, ray, and intersect to orally explain why the figures are perpendicular.
key_questions: How are perpendicular and intersecting lines similar and different? How do you know when two lines are perpendicular?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students define the term perpendicular and identify perpendicular lines and line segments in real-world objects. Students draw perpendicular line segments and identify them in polygons. They use symbols to write statements indicating one line or line segment is perpendicular to another line or line segment. This lesson formalizes the terms intersect and perpendicular.

title: Identify, define, and draw parallel lines.
objectives: Identify, define, and draw parallel lines.
i_can: I can name and draw lines that will never intersect.
language_objectives: Write statements to identify and name two parallel lines, rays, or line segments by using the parallel symbol. Use terms such as parallel, line, line segment, ray, and intersect to orally explain why the figures are parallel. Orally identify an error in sample work about identifying two parallel line segments, and explain how to correct the error.
key_questions: How do you know when two lines are parallel?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students define the term parallel and identify parallel lines, line segments, and rays in real-world objects. Students draw parallel line segments and identify them in polygons. They use symbols to write statements indicating that one line, line segment, or ray is parallel to another line, line segment, or ray.

title: Relate geometric figures to a real-world context.
objectives: Relate geometric figures to a real-world context.
i_can: I can find examples of figures in a floor plan.
language_objectives: Orally explain the thought process and strategies used when deciding what questions to ask to identify the figure that was chosen from a collection by a partner. Listen to descriptions of floor plans with geometric figures and orally compare the floor plans. Write to describe geometric features of a figure by using precise terminology.
key_questions: Why is it useful to be precise when describing figures? Where can you find examples of figures in the real world?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.", "Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.
laag: Students use precise geometric terminology to identify a specific geometric figure from a set of figures. They use geometric figures to draw a floor plan of a dream home and relate geometric figures to the real-world context of a home. There is no Problem Set in this lesson. Instead, use classroom observations and the classwork to analyze student thinking after the lesson.

title: Explore angles as fractional turns through a circle.
objectives: Explore angles as fractional turns through a circle.
i_can: I can name angle types and fractions of a circle.
language_objectives: Use terms such as acute angle, right angle, obtuse angle, straight angle, and reflex angle to orally name the angle types shown when using an angle-maker tool to make fractional turns through a circle.
key_questions: How are angles and fractions of a circle related?
big_idea: Circles, Fractions, and Decimals Shapes and Symmetries
ad_texts: ["Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)"]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD1] Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)
laag: Students construct an angle-maker tool by using two cardstock circles. They use the tool to make angles of various sizes and see that an angle can be understood as a fractional turn through a circle. This lesson formalizes the term reflex angle.

title: Use a circular protractor to recognize a 1 degree angle as a turn through 1/360 of a circle.
objectives: Use a circular protractor to recognize a 1 degree angle as a turn through 1/360 of a circle.
i_can: I can measure angles with a protractor.
language_objectives: Use terms such as degree, acute angle, right angle, obtuse angle, straight angle, and reflex angle to orally describe a benchmark angle as both a number of degrees and a fraction of a turn through a circle.
key_questions: What is a protractor used for?
ad_texts: ["Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)", "Measure and draw angles in degrees."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD1] Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b) [4.Mod6.AD2] Measure and draw angles in degrees.
laag: Students use their angle-maker tools and circular protractors to make and measure angles of various sizes. They use a protractor to see that a turn through of a circle is the same measure as a angle. Students begin to recognize benchmark angles and describe them as a number of degrees and as a fraction of a turn through a circle. This lesson formalizes the term degree.

title: Identify and measure angles as turns and recognize them in various contexts.
objectives: Identify and measure angles as turns and recognize them in various contexts.
i_can: I can identify and measure angles as turns.
language_objectives: Use terms such as quarter turn, half turn, three-quarter turn, clockwise, counterclockwise, and whole turn to orally describe movements of the minute hand on a clock in terms of angle measures and degrees. Listen to and follow instructions that kinesthetically relate the number of degrees turned to the directions north, south, east, and west.
key_questions: How can we measure turns? How is turning your body similar to the hands turning on a clock?
ad_texts: ["Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)"]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD1] Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)
laag: Students relate the turns made by clock hands to angles, which can be measured by using degrees. Similarly, students see that turning their body to face different directions can also be described by using degrees. Students use degrees in relation to directions.

title: Use protractors to measure 180° angles.
objectives: Use protractors to measure 180° angles.
i_can: I can measure angles with a different kind of protractor.
language_objectives: With a partner, orally describe how to use a protractor to measure angles.
key_questions: How do we use a protractor to measure angles?
ad_texts: ["Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)", "Measure and draw angles in degrees.", "Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD1] Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b) [4.Mod6.AD2] Measure and draw angles in degrees. laag: Students identify angles as right, acute, obtuse, or straight and use a protractor to find the angle measure. They use their knowledge of types of angles to reason about which scale on the protractor to use for the given angle.

title: Estimate and measure 180° angles with a protractor.
objectives: Estimate and measure 180° angles with a protractor.
i_can: estimate and measure angles with a I can protractor.
language_objectives: Orally explain the thought process and strategies used to match angle measure cards with the correct angle measures.
key_questions: Why is estimation helpful when measuring angles? How can two angles that look different have the same measure?
ad_texts: ["Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b)", "Measure and draw angles in degrees.", "Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD1] Convert between angle measures expressed as a fractional turn through a circle and degrees. (4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.5.a, 4.MD.C.5.b) [4.Mod6.AD2] Measure and draw angles in degrees. [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.
laag: Students determine that angles can have rays of different lengths and still have the same angle measure. They use estimation to make sense of the measure of an angle and then precisely measure angles by using protractors, extending the rays if needed.

title: Use a protractor to draw angles up to 180°.
objectives: Use a protractor to draw angles up to 180°.
i_can: I can use a protractor to accurately draw angles.
language_objectives: Orally identify an error in sample work about a drawn angle and explain how to correct the error. Orally describe how to use a protractor to draw angles up to and justify whether angle drawings are reasonable.
key_questions: What tools can help us draw angles accurately? How can estimating an angle measure help determine whether a drawing is reasonable?
ad_texts: ["Measure and draw angles in degrees.", "Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD2] Measure and draw angles in degrees. [4.Mod6.AD4] Identify and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines.
laag: Students draw angles by using a protractor. Before drawing an angle, students think about the type of the angle and the size of the angle in relation to a benchmark angle. They sketch the angle and then use a protractor and a straightedge to accurately draw the angle.

title: Decompose angles by using pattern blocks.
objectives: Decompose angles by using pattern blocks.
i_can: I can decompose larger angles into smaller angles to find angle measurements.
language_objectives: Orally compare solution strategies for finding the unknown measure of an angle by first using pattern blocks to decompose the angle into smaller angles and then adding the measures of the smaller angles together.
key_questions: How can angles be decomposed? How can decomposing an angle help find the measure of the angle?
ad_texts: ["Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD3] Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction.
laag: Students use known angle measures of pattern blocks to find other angle measures in pattern blocks. They decompose angles into smaller known angles by using pattern blocks and then add the measures of smaller angles to find the unknown measure of a larger angle.

title: Find unknown angle measures within right and straight angles.
objectives: Find unknown angle measures within right and straight angles.
i_can: I can use right angles and straight angles to find unknown angle measurements.
language_objectives: Use terms such as complementary angles, adjacent angles, and supplementary angles to orally describe how to find an unknown angle measure when given two angles that are complementary or supplementary.
key_questions: What strategies can we use to find an unknown angle measure when a right angle or straight angle is decomposed into smaller angles?
ad_texts: ["Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD3] Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction.
laag: Students fold paper to decompose right and straight angles and then write related addition equations. They find an unknown angle measure when the total angle measure and one part is known. This lesson formalizes the terms adjacent angles, complementary angles, and supplementary angles.

title: Find unknown angle measures within a decomposed angle of up to 180°.
objectives: Find unknown angle measures within a decomposed angle of up to 180°.
i_can: I can choose strategies to find unknown angle measurements.
language_objectives: Write or draw to record how to find an unknown angle measure when a straight angle is decomposed into smaller angles. Listen to and orally describe solution strategies—including count on, subtract from the total, and add then subtract—to find an unknown angle measure within a decomposed straight angle, and compare and connect solution strategies.
key_questions: How can we use addition or subtraction to find an unknown angle measure? How can we use the decomposed parts of an angle to find the total angle measure?
ad_texts: ["Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD3] Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction.
laag: Students fold paper to decompose right and straight angles into three parts and write related addition equations. They find unknown angle measures when benchmark and nonbenchmark angles are decomposed into two or more parts.

title: Find unknown angle measures around a point.
objectives: Find unknown angle measures around a point.
i_can: I can find multiple unknown angles measures around a point.
language_objectives: Orally explain how to find the measures of multiple unknown angles around a point.
key_questions: What are some ways we can find the measure of an angle without using a protractor? How can knowing the angle measures of adjacent angles help us find unknown angle measures?
ad_texts: ["Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD3] Solve for unknown angle measures by using addition and subtraction.
laag: Students find unknown angle measures within angles measuring greater than and unknown angle measures where the sum of the angles is They use addition, subtraction, or both addition and subtraction, to find each angle measure.

title: Recognize, identify, and draw lines of symmetry.
objectives: Recognize, identify, and draw lines of symmetry.
i_can: I can identify and draw lines of symmetry.
language_objectives: Use terms such as line of symmetry, horizontal, and vertical to orally analyze attributes of both geometric figures and pictures of real-life objects. Use the attributes to recognize, orally identify, and draw lines of symmetry. Orally describe how to complete a drawing of a figure when given the line of symmetry and only half of the figure.
key_questions: How do you recognize lines of symmetry in figures? Where do you see lines of symmetry in real-world objects?
ad_texts: ["Identify and draw lines of symmetry."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD7] Identify and draw lines of symmetry.
laag: Students identify lines of symmetry on geometric figures and on pictures of real-world objects. They draw lines of symmetry and recognize attributes of shapes that affect symmetry. They also complete drawings of figures when the line of symmetry and only half of the figure are given. This lesson formalizes the term line of symmetry.

title: Analyze and classify triangles based on side length, angle measures, or both.
objectives: Analyze and classify triangles based on side length, angle measures, or both.
i_can: I can classify triangles.
language_objectives: Use terms such as acute triangle, obtuse triangle, right triangle, equilateral triangle, isosceles triangle, and scalene triangle to orally justify classifying a triangle based on side lengths and angle measures.
key_questions: What information is needed to classify a triangle? What tools or symbols are helpful when classifying triangles?
ad_texts: ["Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.", "Identify attributes and use them to two-dimensional classify figures, including triangles."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures. [4.Mod6.AD6] Identify attributes and use them to two-dimensional classify figures, including triangles.
laag: Students construct a triangle and classify triangles based on their attributes. They use rulers, right-angle tools, and symbols in drawings to help them. This lesson formalizes the terms acute triangle, obtuse triangle, right triangle, equilateral triangle, isosceles triangle, and scalene triangle.

title: Construct and classify triangles based on given attributes.
objectives: Construct and classify triangles based on given attributes.
i_can: I can draw triangles based on their descriptions.
language_objectives: Orally hypothesize about whether a scalene triangle can have two right angles or two obtuse angles, and draw to support the thinking. Orally justify why given statements about equilateral triangles are always, sometimes, or never true.
key_questions: What tools are helpful when drawing triangles? When drawing a triangle with certain angles and side lengths, how do you determine what to draw first—the side length or the angle type?
ad_texts: ["Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures.", "Identify attributes and use them to classify two-dimensional figures, including triangles."]
ad_full: [4.Mod6.AD5] Identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines in two-dimensional figures. [4.Mod6.AD6] Identify attributes and use them to classify two-dimensional figures, including triangles.
laag: Students use a protractor and a ruler to draw triangles when given a triangle classification. They make a model of an equilateral triangle and use the model to reason about the attributes of an equilateral triangle. Students reason about what angle types can be used to compose a triangle.

title: Sort polygons based on a given rule.

title: Solve word problems involving perimeter, area, and volume.
objectives: Solve word problems involving perimeter, area, and volume.
i_can: I can solve word problems that involve perimeter, area, and volume.
language_objectives: Read word problems involving perimeter, area, and volume, and orally justify a solution strategy by using language from the problem that indicates which measurement to find. Write or draw to record a solution strategy and an equation to solve a problem involving perimeter, area, and volume.
key_questions: How do you know whether a situation involves perimeter, area, or volume?
ad_texts: ["Calculate volumes of right rectangular prisms by using and", "Find volumes of figures composed of right rectangular prisms to solve real-world and mathematical problems."]
ad_full: [5.Mod5.AD11] Calculate volumes of right rectangular prisms by using and [5.Mod5.AD12] Find volumes of figures composed of right rectangular prisms to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
laag: Students work in pairs to sort real-world situations into categories based on whether the situations require finding perimeter, area, or volume. When students consider the length of wood that encloses a garden box, the amount of the lawn a garden box covers, and the amount of soil needed to fill a garden box, they recognize that building a garden box requires finding all three measurements: perimeter, area, and volume. Students choose real-world problems to solve: one involving perimeter, one involving area, and one involving volume.

title: Apply concepts and formulas of volume to design a sculpture by using right rectangular prisms, part 1.
objectives: Apply concepts and formulas of volume to design a sculpture by using right rectangular prisms, part 1.
i_can: I can use right rectangular prisms to design a sculpture and to find its volume.
language_objectives: Read the guidelines for creating a sculpture and orally discuss the guidelines and ideas for a design with a partner. Through listening to and speaking with a partner, design and create a sculpture that meets the guidelines by using the formula for volume to calculate the dimensions of the prisms in the sculpture.
key_questions: How can you create a right rectangular prism that is a fraction of the volume of another prism?
ad_texts: ["Calculate volumes of right rectangular prisms by using and", "Find volumes of figures composed of right rectangular prisms to solve real-world and mathematical problems. (5 . M D . C . 5.c)"]

laag: Students design and create a sculpture inspired by a piece of art called Cubi VI. While following guidelines for creating a sculpture, students choose heights for right rectangular prisms with given bases and multiply edge lengths to calculate volumes. Students work in pairs to assemble several prisms and use the prisms to create sculptures. Partners record their calculations for the total volume of their sculptures to be used in the next lesson. There is no Problem Set for this lesson. Instead, students use the time to complete their sculptures and record their calculations.

title: Apply concepts and formulas of volume to design a sculpture by using right rectangular prisms, part 2.
objectives: Apply concepts and formulas of volume to design a sculpture by using right rectangular prisms, part 2.
i_can: I can analyze and discuss my classmates sculptures.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, critique a classmate’s sculpture to determine if it meets the guidelines given in the previous lesson. In partners, read classmates’ critiques of the sculpture. Orally and in writing, reflect on the critiques by discussing whether anything should change in the sculpture.
key_questions: How is reviewing someone else’s sculpture and calculations different from creating your own sculpture that meets given guidelines?
ad_texts: ["Calculate volumes of right rectangular prisms by using and", "Find volumes of figures composed of right rectangular prisms to solve real-world and mathematical problems."]
ad_full: [5.Mod5.AD11] Calculate volumes of right rectangular prisms by using and [5.Mod5.AD12] Find volumes of figures composed of right rectangular prisms to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
laag: As a class, students describe, analyze, interpret, and discuss a sculpture to check that it meets the guidelines for the sculpture given in the previous lesson. Then students observe to review and critique elements of their classmates’ sculptures. Students reflect about whether they would change their own sculptures and, if so, in what ways. There is no Problem Set for this lesson. Instead, students use that time for analysis and discussion of their peers’ sculptures.

title: Construct a coordinate system on a line.
objectives: Construct a coordinate system on a line.
i_can: I can construct a coordinate system on a line.
language_objectives: Listen to and read different ways to describe the location of a point on a number line by using a coordinate system and to plot the point. Orally describe the location of a point on a number line by using a coordinate system and the term coordinate.
key_questions: How is a coordinate system on a line useful? What is important to remember when constructing a coordinate system on a line?
ad_texts: ["Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD3] Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system.
laag: Students construct a coordinate system on a line by marking an interval length as unit and then repeatedly marking the unit a number of times from They use a coordinate to describe and identify a point’s location on a line, and they plot a point on a line given either its coordinate or its distance in units from another point. This lesson formalizes the terms coordinate and coordinate system.

title: Construct a coordinate system in a plane.
objectives: Construct a coordinate system in a plane.
i_can: I can plot points in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally describe the location of a point in a plane by using a coordinate system and the terms and ordered pair. Read a sequence of steps to construct a coordinate plane and to plot points in a plane when given ordered pairs or descriptions of the locations of the points.
key_questions: How is a coordinate system in a plane useful? What is important to remember when plotting a point in the coordinate plane?
ad_texts: ["Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD3] Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system.
laag: Students construct a coordinate system in a plane and use the coordinate system to describe the location of a point plotted in the plane. Students use a point’s horizontal and vertical distances from the axes to identify its ordered pair. After labeling a coordinate plane, students plot points when given ordered pairs. This lesson introduces the terms axes, coordinate plane, ordered pair, and origin.

title: Identify and plot points by using ordered pairs.
objectives: Identify and plot points by using ordered pairs.
i_can: I can use ordered pairs to identify and plot points in a coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally describe how to identify the ordered pair for a point plotted in a coordinate plane by using the interval length of each axis and the point’s distance from each axis. Orally justify an interval length chosen for the axes of a coordinate plane by analyzing the coordinates of a given set of points.
key_questions: What does an or of indicate about the location of a point in a coordinate plane? Why do we use interval lengths other than to label grid lines?
ad_texts: ["Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD3] Plot and interpret points in a two-dimensional coordinate system.
laag: Students construct a coordinate system and use ordered pairs to describe the location of points on axes in the coordinate plane. Given coordinate planes in which the axes have interval lengths other than students write the coordinates of points as ordered pairs and use coordinates to plot points.

title: Describe the distance and direction between points in the coordinate plane.
objectives: Describe the distance and direction between points in the coordinate plane.
i_can: I can describe the distance and direction between points in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, describe how to move from one point to another on a map in a coordinate plane by using the number of units north, south, up, or down and the number of units east, west, right, or left between the points. Listen to and read descriptions of movement between points in a coordinate plane to identify the locations of the points.
key_questions: How can we describe movement between points in the coordinate plane? When we move from one point to another point in the coordinate plane, how are the ordered pairs for the two points different?
ad_texts: ["Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.", "Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD4] Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students use a digital interactive to describe the locations of points on a map in the coordinate plane, and they describe the movement between those points in terms of distance and direction. Students describe distance in units by using the directions left and right, west and east, up and down, and north and south.

title: Identify properties of horizontal and vertical lines.
objectives: Identify properties of horizontal and vertical lines.
i_can: I can identify properties of horizontal and vertical lines.
language_objectives: Read statements about horizontal and vertical lines to determine whether the statements are true or false, and orally justify the decisions. Read directions about how to draw and label lines in a coordinate plane. Plot points on the line and write an ordered pair for each point.
key_questions: Why do points on a horizontal line have the same Why do points on a vertical line have the same How is the coordinate plane useful for reasoning about horizontal and vertical lines?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students work with a partner to draw a coordinate plane, plot points that lie on vertical or horizontal lines, and make conjectures about those lines. Students discover that all points on a horizontal line have the same because they are all the same distance from the and all points on a vertical line have the same because they are all the same distance from the Students determine whether horizontal and vertical lines are parallel or perpendicular to one another or to the axes.

title: Use properties of horizontal and vertical lines to solve problems.
objectives: Use properties of horizontal and vertical lines to solve problems.
i_can: I can use the properties of horizontal and vertical lines to solve problems.
language_objectives: Read directions to plot, draw, and label points and lines in a coordinate plane by using properties of horizontal and vertical lines.
key_questions: How do we determine the distance between two vertical or two horizontal lines? What does a shaded region in the coordinate plane represent?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students use properties of horizontal and vertical lines to solve mathematical problems, such as drawing a line when given information about points on the line and determining the distance between parallel lines. Then students use horizontal and vertical lines to divide the plane into regions. Students identify regions based on descriptions and explain what coordinates of points in those regions have in common. title: Generate number patterns to form ordered pairs.
objectives: Generate number patterns to form ordered pairs.
i_can: I can write ordered pairs to represent number patterns.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, describe the rule for a given number pattern and generate new numbers in the pattern. Orally relate patterns in the coordinates of ordered pairs in a table to patterns in the locations of points in a coordinate plane.
key_questions: How do the rules for number patterns help us plot points with corresponding terms in the coordinate plane?

laag: Students use a starting number and a rule to generate the terms of a number pattern. Then students use two number patterns to extend their understanding of patterns to the coordinate plane. They generate two number patterns in tables and form ordered pairs. After graphing the ordered pairs, students explore how patterns between the locations of points relate to number patterns in the table.

title: Identify addition and subtraction relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns.
objectives: Identify addition and subtraction relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns.
i_can: I can identify addition and subtraction relationships between coordinates of points and pairs. use those relationships to write ordered
language_objectives: Identify a relationship between in a table and use the relationship to orally explain how to find unknown coordinates. Orally and in writing, describe how to move from one point to the next in a coordinate plane.
key_questions: Why is the addition rule for both number patterns the same when there is an addition or subtraction relationship between and Why is it useful to know when and have an addition or subtraction relationship?

laag: Students generate coordinates of points from two number patterns that use the same addition rule, form ordered pairs, and plot the points in the coordinate plane. When they recognize that the movement right is the same number of units as the movement up from one point to the next, they see where the addition rules are represented in the graph. Students identify addition and subtraction relationships between coordinates and apply the relationship to find one coordinate when they know its corresponding coordinate.

title: Identify multiplication and division relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns.
objectives: Identify multiplication and division relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns.
i_can: I can identify multiplication and division relationships between coordinates of points and pairs. use those relationships to write ordered
language_objectives: Orally justify whether a statement about number patterns in a table of coordinates is true or false by reasoning about the rules for the coordinates. Orally and in writing, describe a multiplication and division relationship between corresponding and by using the addition rule for each coordinate.
key_questions: What do you need to know to generate corresponding terms of two number patterns? Why is it useful to know when and have a multiplication or division relationship?

laag: Students generate coordinates of points from two number patterns that use different addition rules. They form ordered pairs from the patterns and plot points in the coordinate plane. Students identify multiplication and division relationships between coordinates and apply the relationship to find one coordinate when they know its corresponding coordinate.

title: Identify mixed-operation relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns. (Optional)
objectives: Identify mixed-operation relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns. (Optional)
i_can: I can identify relationships between coordinates that have more than one operation.
language_objectives: With a partner, listen to and orally describe relationships between corresponding terms in two number patterns and make connections to points in a coordinate plane.
key_questions: How do the addition rules used to generate patterns of coordinates help you determine the relationship between coordinates?

laag: Students plot points and compare two tables of number patterns generated by the same two addition rules but with different starting numbers. One table has a multiplication relationship between coordinates, and one has a mixed-operation relationship between coordinates. They plot points and compare the locations of each set of points in the coordinate plane. Students recognize how the addition rules used to generate terms in the number patterns can help them determine a mixed-operation relationship between corresponding terms. In groups, students match coordinates represented in tables and graphs to a mixed-operation relationship between corresponding terms.

title: Draw lines in the coordinate plane and identify points on the lines.
objectives: Draw lines in the coordinate plane and identify points on the lines.
i_can: I can draw lines in the coordinate plane and identify points on lines.
language_objectives: Orally justify why a point lies on a line by using the relationship between the and of points on the line and patterns or addition rules within each coordinate. Listen to reasoning about why a point lies on a line to support the reasoning or to correct an error in the reasoning.
key_questions: What methods can you use to identify the ordered pairs for points on a line?
ad_texts: ["Generate and represent numerical patterns by using tables and the coordinate plane.", "Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD2] Generate and represent numerical patterns by using tables and the coordinate plane. [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students determine that there are an infinite number of lines through one point but only one line through two points. After identifying various ordered pairs for points on a line, students recognize that a line is composed of an infinite number of points and that the relationship between the and is the same for every point on the line. Students then use a variety of methods to identify ordered pairs for points on a line.

title: Graph and classify quadrilaterals in the coordinate plane.
objectives: Graph and classify quadrilaterals in the coordinate plane.
i_can: I can graph and classify quadrilaterals in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: In groups, orally classify quadrilaterals in the coordinate plane by using the ordered pairs of each vertex and the properties of quadrilaterals.
key_questions: How can you use the coordinate plane to help you classify a quadrilateral?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.", "Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. [5.Mod5.AD14] Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.
laag: Students draw line segments, angles, and quadrilaterals in the coordinate plane. They count units or subtract coordinates to determine the lengths of vertical and horizontal line segments. When one of an angle’s rays is on a horizontal or vertical grid line, students determine whether the angle is right, acute, or obtuse by comparing the angle’s other ray to a perpendicular grid line and by using a protractor. Students use the conclusions they draw about angles to classify quadrilaterals graphed in the coordinate plane.

title: Draw symmetric figures in the coordinate plane.
objectives: Draw symmetric figures in the coordinate plane.
i_can: I can draw symmetric figures in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, describe how the and of pairs of symmetric points in a figure are related by using each point’s distance from the line of symmetry. Read a sequence of steps to plot points and to draw line segments in the coordinate plane and then connect the points and line segments to make symmetric figures. Orally explain the methods used to identify the locations of the points.
key_questions: What is the same and what is different about symmetric points, line segments, and angles in the coordinate plane? How do you draw a symmetric figure in the coordinate plane?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students identify lines of symmetry in a piece of geometric art, and then they use horizontal and vertical lines in the coordinate plane as lines of symmetry. Students plot points that are symmetric and notice similarities and differences between points on either side of lines of symmetry, progressing to drawing symmetric figures composed of line segments and angles. There is no Problem Set for this lesson. Instead, students complete a teacher-guided activity in which they create a symmetric drawing and explore all the aspects of symmetry in the coordinate plane.

title: Solve mathematical problems with rectangles in the coordinate plane.
objectives: Solve mathematical problems with rectangles in the coordinate plane.
i_can: I can solve problems with rectangles in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally describe methods to determine the locations of the unknown vertices of a rectangle in the coordinate plane by applying knowledge of rectangles and symmetry and by plotting points in the coordinate plane.
key_questions: What methods can you use to locate a rectangle’s vertices in the coordinate plane?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. ( 5 . G . A . 2)"]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. ( 5 . G . A . 2)
laag: Students apply their understanding of the properties of rectangles to solve mathematical problems in the coordinate plane. When given information about vertices, symmetry, or side lengths of rectangles, students choose the best method with which to determine locations of other vertices. Students identify similarities and differences in ordered pairs for vertices and explain why it is possible to have several different rectangles with the same length and width that share a common vertex.

title: Use the coordinate plane to reason about perimeters and areas of rectangles.
objectives: Use the coordinate plane to reason about perimeters and areas of rectangles.
i_can: I can find the perimeter and area of a rectangle in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally explain how to find the perimeter of a rectangle in the coordinate plane by counting the number of units of each side length or by finding the difference between or of vertices. Orally explain where to plot two points in a coordinate plane to complete a rectangle with a given perimeter.
key_questions: How can we find the perimeter of a rectangle graphed in the coordinate plane? How can we find the area of a rectangle graphed in the coordinate plane?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.", "Find areas of rectangles and figures composed of rectangles with fraction or mixed-number side lengths."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. [5.Mod5.AD3] Find areas of rectangles and figures composed of rectangles with fraction or mixed-number side lengths.
laag: Students work with a partner to determine the perimeters and areas of rectangles graphed in the coordinate plane. They compare methods for making these calculations when the axis intervals are not By interpreting scales, using the grid, and calculating distance, students use the structure of the coordinate plane to solve mathematical problems.

title: Interpret graphs that represent real-world situations.
objectives: Interpret graphs that represent real-world situations.
i_can: I can interpret graphs that represent real-world situations.
language_objectives: Listen to arguments about which graph shows the relationship between two units of measurement and orally justify which graph shows the correct relationship. Orally and in writing, describe the meaning of a point in a graph that represents a real- world situation by interpreting the point within the context of the situation.
key_questions: How is the coordinate plane a useful tool for representing real-world situations?
ad_texts: ["Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.", "Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD4] Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane. [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: This lesson introduces students to another application of the coordinate plane: representing data. Students learn how graphs can tell a story. Building on their previous work with bar graphs, students use the coordinate plane to represent and interpret real-world situations. They identify coordinates of points, interpret the real-world meaning of and and plot points.

title: Plot data in the coordinate plane and analyze relationships.
objectives: Plot data in the coordinate plane and analyze relationships.
i_can: I can represent and analyze data in the coordinate plane.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, interpret the meaning of points in a graph by using the context of the situation and what the and represent. Orally and in writing, draw conclusions about the points represented in a graph by using the context of the situation and what each axis represents. Read information in a table or graph to determine the meaning of the points and the story the data show.
key_questions: Why is it useful to represent data as points plotted in the coordinate plane?
ad_texts: ["Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD4] Solve real-world problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students perform a data collection activity twice, in two different ways. As a class, they realize that they cannot use a bar graph to represent the data; instead, they form ordered pairs and represent the data by plotting points in the coordinate plane. Students make observations and draw conclusions based on the locations of points in the coordinate plane. In groups, students collect and analyze another set of data. There is no Problem Set for this lesson. Instead, there are problems for students to complete in small groups.

title: Interpret line graphs.
objectives: Interpret line graphs.
i_can: I can interpret line graphs.
language_objectives: Orally and in writing, interpret the meaning of points and line segments in a graph by using the context of the situation and what the and represent. Orally and in writing, describe a story that a line graph represents by interpreting the trend indicated by the line segments.
key_questions: Why is a line graph a useful tool for representing data? How do we interpret a line graph?
ad_texts: ["Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane."]
ad_full: [5.Mod6.AD5] Solve mathematical problems by using the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
laag: Students analyze and interpret line graphs that represent real-world data, and they use points from the graphs to support their thinking. Students learn that the line segments on a line graph show trends and not actual data. They explain stories that a variety of graphs tell. Students use the Five Framing Questions routine to analyze distance–time graphs.

title: Reason about visual patterns by using tables and graphs. (Optional)
objectives: Reason about visual patterns by using tables and graphs. (Optional)

laag: Students apply their understanding of relationships between corresponding terms in number patterns to identify and analyze relationships in visual patterns. title: Reason about patterns in real-world situations.
objectives: Reason about patterns in real-world situations.
i_can: I can reason about patterns in real-world situations.
language_objectives: Write or draw to record a strategy for determining the total number of nickels collected for a fundraiser, including using a graph, a table, or an addition relationship. key_questions: How can we use what we know to solve real-world problems?

laag: Students watch a video about a fundraiser, create a list of questions about the video, and select one focus question to answer. title: Jars of Jelly Beans
objectives: Use multiplicative reasoning to estimate the solution to a real-world problem.

language_objectives: Orally explain and listen to estimation strategies as a class and in smaller groups.
key_questions: How can we use multiplicative reasoning to model situations and solve real-world problems?

ad_full: [6.Mod1.AD3] Solve real-world and mathematical problems by using ratio reasoning.

This lesson is designed as a formative assessment for several Standards for Mathematical Practice. There is an optional extension to challenge students.

title: Introduction to Ratios
objectives: Write ratios that relate two quantities as an ordered pair of numbers. Use ratio language to compare two quantities.
i_can: I can use ratio language to compare two quantities.
language_objectives: Read ratios and orally describe them by using ratio language and multiplicative comparison language.
key_questions: What is a ratio? When is it more practical to use ratio language instead of multiplicative comparison language?

ad_texts: ["Write and explain ratios that describe relationships between two quantities."]
ad_full: [6.Mod1.AD1] Write and explain ratios that describe relationships between two quantities.
laag: In this lesson, students discuss their reactions to a video, which introduces the need to use new language to compare two quantities.
